storefrontOverrides.purpose: An override applies a different active state, mode or template set for one StoreKit storefront country code.

actions.1: Add a canonical three-letter storefront code and configure only the intended difference.
actions.2: Remove an override to return that storefront to the global fallback.

storefrontOverrides.guidance: Storefront is read when the app opens this screen and is not written to the member profile. It may differ from residence or current location.

inviteResults.title: Invite results
inviteResults.purpose: The read-only conversion summary Core builds from recorded invitations: the totals, the split by delivery mode, and the inviting members with their own recorded and converted counts.

actions.1: Read the totals before changing a delivery mode, so a later drop can be attributed to that change.
actions.2: Open an inviting member from the table when a support question is about their invitations.

inviteResults.guidance: Counts only — no phone number or recipient identity is served or shown. Unconverted invitations expire, so the expiring-within-seven-days figure explains a fall that is not a product failure. The table is the first page of senders while the totals describe the whole collection, and the panel prints one muted line instead of failing when Core cannot build the summary.

support.title: Support inbox help
support.summary: The Support inbox contains one direct operations conversation per member. Replies can reach the member through the in-app bell, realtime delivery and background push, while recent client context helps diagnose app-specific problems.

steps.1: Select the correct member thread by name and UID and read the full recent conversation before replying.
steps.2: Open Client details only for diagnostic context and inspect images only when the support case requires it.
steps.3: Send one clear response or normalized image and wait for a definitive result before retrying.

threadList.title: Member thread list
threadList.purpose: Rows show member identity, latest message, source platform, time and the operator-side unread count for each support conversation.

actions.1: Choose a thread by confirmed UID, not display name alone.
actions.2: Use unread badges and latest activity to prioritize pending support.

threadList.guidance: Opening a conversation clears the operator-side unread counter. Read the thread before switching away so work is not mistaken for completed support.

conversation.title: Conversation history
conversation.purpose: The message timeline separates member and administrator messages, text and image events, platform labels and delivery chronology.

actions.1: Read prior answers and member-provided context before composing a reply.
actions.2: Open a retained image in the protected lightbox when its content is relevant.

conversation.guidance: A removed image remains as a terminal event and must not be treated as a loading error. Avoid repeating advice already given in the thread.

clientContext.title: Client details
clientContext.purpose: The latest bounded context can show source platform, app or build information, device and accessibility settings useful for reproducing a problem.

actions.1: Expand diagnostics when the issue depends on Android, iOS or Web behavior.
actions.2: Use facts such as build and appearance settings to route or reproduce the report.

clientContext.guidance: Client context is diagnostic, may be absent or stale, and is not proof of member identity. Do not expose internal device detail unnecessarily in the reply.

attachments.title: Support images
attachments.purpose: Authorized image messages are served through a trusted media boundary, and outbound files are normalized to bounded, metadata-free JPEG before Core receives them.

actions.1: Open an inbound image only for the active support task.
actions.2: Attach a supported JPEG, PNG or WebP when a visual answer is genuinely useful, and reuse the offered retry after a known failed response.

attachments.guidance: Images may contain private member information. Do not download, reuse or forward them outside the conversation, and do not send credentials or private evidence.

reply.title: Compose and send
reply.purpose: The composer sends bounded text or one image to the selected UID and triggers the supported member notification channels.

actions.1: Write a direct, non-technical response with a clear next step.
actions.2: Send once, or use the exact preserved image retry when the UI offers it.

reply.guidance: A timeout can leave delivery uncertain. Re-read the conversation before creating a second logical message, especially when the first response may have landed.

helpCms.title: Help centre CMS guide
helpCms.summary: This CMS publishes the member-facing Friending Help centre. Categories organize discovery, while each article stores English and Hungarian title, summary, search keywords and a structured block body that publishes as one bilingual unit.

steps.1: Choose or create the category first, then open one article draft by its permanent slug.
steps.2: Complete and proofread both locale tabs, including structure, links, emphasis and warnings.
steps.3: Save a private draft for review or publish only when both languages are complete; archive obsolete articles instead of reusing their identity.

articleEditor.title: Article editor
articleEditor.purpose: The editor brings permanent identity, category, discovery settings, locale content and block structure into one versioned draft.

actions.1: Create a new article or open an existing draft, published or archived article.
actions.2: Save without publishing, or publish after the whole bilingual document passes validation.

articleEditor.guidance: Save draft is private; Publish is member-visible. A published correction goes live as one article, so review the complete result rather than only the changed sentence.

metadata.title: Slug, category and featured rank
metadata.purpose: The slug is permanent article identity, the category controls Help-home grouping, and featured rank can promote selected articles.

actions.1: Choose a clear lowercase slug when creating the article.
actions.2: Assign the correct category and use a positive featured rank only for intentional Help-home promotion.

metadata.guidance: Lower positive ranks appear first; zero means not featured. Never repurpose an existing slug for unrelated guidance because links and search history may depend on it.

languages.title: English and Hungarian content
languages.purpose: Each locale has its own member-facing title, summary, search keywords and body blocks while sharing one article lifecycle.

actions.1: Switch between EN and HU and provide equivalent, natural guidance in each.
actions.2: Add concise keywords that help member search without appearing in the article.

languages.guidance: Publishing requires both languages. Translate the intended action and product meaning, not just individual words or internal technical names.

contentBlocks.title: Structured content blocks
contentBlocks.purpose: Paragraphs, headings, lists, callouts and other bounded blocks build a readable article without accepting arbitrary HTML.

actions.1: Add the appropriate block type, edit its runs or list items and reorder it with the arrow controls.
actions.2: Apply supported emphasis, links and warning tones only where they improve comprehension.

contentBlocks.guidance: Keep steps task-oriented for members unfamiliar with Friending. Do not place secrets, private evidence links or unsupported markup in article content.

categories.title: Help categories
categories.purpose: Categories provide bilingual Help-home titles and summaries, stable key, display order, icon identity and active state.

actions.1: Create or edit category presentation in both languages.
actions.2: Reorder or deactivate a category when its collection should stop appearing to members.

categories.guidance: An inactive category disappears from the Help home. Review the articles assigned to it so useful published guidance does not become unexpectedly hard to find.

articleList.title: Article inventory
articleList.purpose: The table shows permanent slug, category, both localized titles, draft or published state and featured rank.

actions.1: Open the exact article for editing and compare both locale titles.
actions.2: Use status and rank to audit what members can currently discover.

articleList.guidance: A draft is never member-visible, and an archived article may retain complete content. Status must be read separately from content completeness.

publishing.title: Publish and archive lifecycle
publishing.purpose: Publish validates both locales and makes the article available; archive removes it from member surfaces while preserving the draft for future revision.

actions.1: Publish only after editorial and product review.
actions.2: Archive obsolete guidance and later republish the same stable article when its original topic returns.

publishing.guidance: Help content can change member behavior immediately. Verify links, instructions and current app terminology on the supported clients before publishing.

configuration.title: Configuration help
configuration.summary: Configuration contains only approved product controls that can change without a deployment. It covers Travel and AreYouIn availability with their teaser modals, the Hey, Footprints and photo-likes switches, sign-in methods and allowed phone countries, reversible feature behavior, Join session timing, iOS appearance, global push delivery, public link origins, presence availability, location access requirements and the complete profile selfie verification member flow (video selfie and gesture photo selfie, with the gesture catalogue).

steps.1: Identify the exact product surface and read its current value, bounds and member consequence.
steps.2: Change one coherent setting group, including both languages where copy is involved.
steps.3: Save, refresh and verify the affected client or operational surface without using an unrelated production mutation as a test.

productControls.title: Allow-listed product controls
productControls.purpose: General settings include reversible switches such as People hero delivery and the isolated demo system, with type and bounds supplied by Core.

actions.1: Review the explanation and current server value for each exposed key.
actions.2: Change only a setting whose product impact and rollback are understood.

productControls.guidance: Turning a feature off normally preserves its records. Demo controls never merge demo and regular users, and a disabled hero response does not delete campaigns.

sectionAvailability.title: Travel and AreYouIn availability
sectionAvailability.purpose: Sets whether released apps present the Travel and AreYouIn sections and their entry points: one global answer per section plus optional overrides for individual App Store storefronts.

actions.1: Read the global answer and every storefront override of both sections, together with the shared revision, before editing.
actions.2: Change a global answer or add, edit or remove a storefront override, then press Save section availability once.
actions.3: After a conflict your edits are kept on top of the newly loaded revision; after an unconfirmed save the stored settings are reloaded. Review them, then save again.

sectionAvailability.guidance: The storefront comes from the App Store, never from the member's location. Saving changes what released apps present for that storefront; the teaser copy below has its own revision and its own save.

featureSwitches.title: Hey, Footprints and photo-likes feature switches
featureSwitches.purpose: This independent, receipted control family governs global Hey, Footprint-badge and photo-like availability. Each command changes one switch, while all three share one authoritative family revision; Visitors is always available.

actions.1: Read every served switch state, its provenance and the shared revision before deciding.
actions.2: Enter a required internal reason and change only the intended switch.
actions.3: After an unknown outcome, retry the retained command or reload for authoritative convergence; never start a second logical command.

featureSwitches.guidance: Hey off removes the Pinger button, profile gesture, Heys tab and Hey notifications. Footprints off removes the Footprint-badge controls, feed, counter and notifications, while visits and Visitors remain available. Photo likes off removes photo-like controls, counters, feed and notifications. Visitors is always available. The three switches share one family revision, but badge settings and general runtime settings do not. Launch posture is an explicit audited choice: Hey on, Footprints off.

authPolicy.title: Sign-in and sign-up methods
authPolicy.purpose: Chooses whether phone and e-mail sign-up and sign-in are offered, globally and through overrides for individual App Store storefronts. Sign in with Apple is always available and cannot be switched off here.

actions.1: Set the global default first; phone and e-mail cannot both be disabled there.
actions.2: Add a storefront override only where that App Store country must differ; it replaces both method values for that storefront.
actions.3: Press Save authentication policy once, and after a conflict review your preserved edits on the new revision before saving again.

authPolicy.guidance: The storefront is supplied by the App Store, never inferred from location. Stored values outside Core's current vocabulary are flagged and must be replaced before the policy can be saved.

phoneCountries.title: Allowed phone countries and number formats
phoneCountries.purpose: Inside the authentication policy, the allowed-country rule decides which countries appear in the app's phone picker and derives the calling-code allow-list Core enforces; optional masks format numbers per calling code.

actions.1: Choose All countries or a selected list globally, and add a storefront country override only where one App Store country needs a different list.
actions.2: Add a number mask only for a calling code the selected countries use; each * is a digit, and an empty mask keeps the app's automatic formatting.

phoneCountries.guidance: Countries and calling codes are saved together with the sign-in methods, so they cannot drift apart. A rule that allows no country leaves that scope without a phone picker entry, and a mask for a code no selected country uses stays stored but inert.

session.title: Join idle session timeout
session.purpose: The idle timeout decides how long a signed-in Join browser stays authenticated after the member's last real interaction.

actions.1: Set a whole number of minutes within the displayed bounds.
actions.2: Balance account security with realistic signup and profile-editing sessions.

session.guidance: Background realtime and polling do not count as activity. A shorter timeout can interrupt members who pause during onboarding or profile work.

appearance.title: iOS appearance mode
appearance.purpose: System follows the device's Light or Dark setting live, while Force Light and Force Dark override it for the whole iOS app.

actions.1: Keep System for member-controlled appearance in normal operation.
actions.2: Use a forced mode only for an explicitly tested product or emergency reason.

appearance.guidance: This affects every iOS screen from launch. Test contrast, media and modals throughout the app before forcing an appearance.

pushDelivery.title: Global push delivery mode
pushDelivery.purpose: The mode enables FCM, OneSignal or both provider channels for Core's provider-agnostic push worker; Both handles eligible channels independently.

actions.1: Confirm current member-registration coverage and provider readiness before narrowing the mode.
actions.2: Save one deliberate mode change, wait for the canonical Core response and verify the operational effect without sending a routine test push.

pushDelivery.guidance: This setting does not register devices, configure provider credentials or prove delivery. After an uncertain response, the page reloads authoritative settings before allowing another gesture.

publicLinks.title: Website and profile-link origins
publicLinks.purpose: The website origin builds browser legal and marketing links; the profile origin mints shareable profile links and QR codes recognized by released apps.

actions.1: Choose only HTTPS origins offered or accepted by the corresponding policy.
actions.2: Verify generated legal links, profile links, QR behavior and browser fallback.

publicLinks.guidance: A profile host also needs support in signed app associated domains for direct app opening. An unknown profile origin can remove the in-app QR experience.

presence.title: Profile presence modes
presence.purpose: Presence configuration decides which availability choices members can use and how bilingual labels explain those modes.

actions.1: Review mandatory and optional modes, counts and current revision.
actions.2: Update localized presentation or availability and confirm any affected-member reconciliation.

presence.guidance: Disabling a mode can rewrite affected member profiles to a safe fallback. Treat it as a data-impacting change, not copy-only configuration.

locationAccess.title: Location access
locationAccess.purpose: Two independent, default-off switches tell compatible iOS apps whether a device location is required before the Nearby tab on People and before signup. The panel has its own revision and its own save.

actions.1: Read both switches, the revision and who saved last before changing anything.
actions.2: Change a switch, press Save location access, and confirm when you are making location required.
actions.3: After a conflict the panel loads the newer revision but the switches keep your unsaved choices: review them, then save again or discard them. After an unconfirmed save, reload before trying again.

locationAccess.guidance: This sets app behavior, it does not enforce anything: Core never checks it, and older iOS versions, Android and the Join website ignore it. Requiring location at signup risks App Store rejection under guideline 5.1.1(iv), so switch it on only for a version App Review has seen behaving this way. Viewers can read the policy but cannot save it.

verificationFlow.title: Profile selfie verification flow
verificationFlow.purpose: This editor owns status cards, introduction, camera guidance, preview, detailed owner messages, challenge prompts, consent and privacy link in both languages and appearances.

actions.1: Review every step as one member journey and keep both required head turns plus an enabled expression.
actions.2: Maintain accurate consent, purpose, retention, withdrawal and deletion copy before enabling the flow.
actions.3: Preview Light and Dark colors and save against the independent verification revision.

verificationFlow.guidance: The flow proves a manual comparison of a video or a gesture photo set with the current photo only. It must not claim identity-document verification, automated liveness or general member safety.

photoCatalogue.title: Gesture catalogue and photo wording
photoCatalogue.purpose: Part of the profile selfie verification panel: the gestures members copy for the gesture photo selfie (English and Hungarian title and instruction, a male and a female example image), how many photos each member takes (1–10), and the eighteen sentences members read in the photo flow.

actions.1: Add gestures until the sufficiency line says the catalogue is enough for a set, and upload both example images for every gesture from this console.
actions.2: Set the photo count and edit the photo wording in both languages, then save; every field that needs fixing is highlighted with its problem.
actions.3: If Core refuses the save because the method is live, add gestures or lower the photo count; the catalogue must always hold at least one full set.

photoCatalogue.guidance: Editing the catalogue changes nothing for members until a scope uses the photo method, which is chosen only on Verification settings. Viewers see the panel read-only. Example images are public in the app, so never use a member's photo as an example.

safetyBoundary.title: Safe configuration boundary
safetyBoundary.purpose: The final notice explains why infrastructure hosts, databases, signing keys, provider credentials and other secrets are intentionally absent from browser editing.

actions.1: Use this page only for the named product controls.
actions.2: Follow the deployment or secret-management procedure for anything outside the allow-list.

safetyBoundary.guidance: A missing infrastructure control is a security property, not an incomplete screen. Never move a secret into Webadmin to make it editable.

sectionTeasers.title: Soft off and the teaser modal
sectionTeasers.purpose: Each switched-off section carries a Hidden switch: on hides Travel or AreYouIn completely, off keeps its entry point visible and opens a bilingual title and description in a modal with a close button.

actions.1: Read the Hidden switch of both sections and the teaser revision before editing anything.
actions.2: Turn Hidden off only for a section you are also switching off, then write a title and description in English and Hungarian, or leave a field blank for the compiled copy.
actions.3: Enter an internal reason and use the teaser save button, which is separate from the section-availability save above.

sectionTeasers.guidance: A teaser is presentation only: the section stays refused server-side, so a member who reaches it another way is still blocked. Nothing is published while the section is available, and nothing at all changes until you save.

welcomeMessage.title: Welcome message for new members
welcomeMessage.purpose: This separately saved panel holds the automatic message every new member finds in their Support conversation right after registering, in Hungarian or in English.

actions.1: Edit the Hungarian and the English text, then press Save welcome message; the next registration already gets the new text.
actions.2: Switch it off and save when new members should no longer get it.
actions.3: If the panel says the saved message is damaged, nobody is getting it: write a new message and save it.

welcomeMessage.guidance: It is on by default. The language follows the signup language: Hungarian signups get the Hungarian text, everyone else the English one. Each member gets it once, only at registration; earlier members are never messaged. It arrives as a support message, so replies show up in the Support inbox. Viewers can read it but cannot save it.

appReview.title: App Review sandbox help
appReview.summary: The sandbox is a deterministic, synthetic account used by platform reviewers to experience a populated Friending app. Core owns its fixed identity, fixture, full deletion and same-UID reprovisioning; Webadmin shows readiness and offers one tightly scoped reset.

steps.1: Confirm the control record, lifecycle and fixture version before interpreting any count or check.
steps.2: Read all count witnesses and readiness checks; one failed check means the sandbox is not ready.
steps.3: Reset only when repair is required, using the exact phrase and durable pending request already retained by the page.

identity.title: Reviewer identity
identity.purpose: When authorized by Core, this area identifies the fixed synthetic reviewer account and shows whether review login is configured without exposing its access code.

actions.1: Confirm the expected fixed UID and synthetic markers when they are projected to your role.
actions.2: Check configuration presence without requesting or revealing the plaintext review code.

identity.guidance: Hidden identity fields are an intentional role boundary. The review code never belongs in browser JavaScript, screenshots, tickets or Git.

control.title: Fixture control and lifecycle
control.purpose: The control record names fixture version, revision, reset state, account lifecycle, media manifest and last converged receipt.

actions.1: Verify that the control is ready, no reset is in progress and lifecycle agrees with the account state.
actions.2: Use revision and receipt information to understand the latest reset or automatic restore.

control.guidance: A reviewer-initiated deletion must use the normal full erasure path. Scheduled recovery then provisions a clean account; Webadmin must not weaken deletion to preserve the fixture.

counts.title: Scoped document witnesses
counts.purpose: The complete census of 23 counts covers profile, media, relationships, chats, notifications, membership, verification and AreYouIn records belonging to the protected fixture scope.

actions.1: Compare every actual count with its expected witness.
actions.2: Use a mismatch to identify which fixture area needs a guarded reset or server investigation.

counts.guidance: Counts alone do not prove meaningful content or valid media. They must be read together with all semantic checks.

checks.title: Readiness checks
checks.purpose: The 34 closed checks prove control, environment match, account state, complete content, valid media, the PLUS and verification grants and AreYouIn semantics.

actions.1: Inspect every failing check and its associated count or lifecycle clue.
actions.2: Claim readiness only when the complete set is green.

checks.guidance: A partial green page is not release-ready. The parser intentionally rejects unknown or incomplete successful payloads rather than hiding missing checks. A muted row is not a failure: the feature behind that check is switched off, so its content is out of the reviewer's reach and the check is not a witness of completeness — readiness stays green without it.

reset.title: Guarded reset to baseline
reset.purpose: Reset transactionally reconciles only the protected fixture and reviewer-keyed runtime rows, then validates post-commit media and product semantics.

actions.1: Read current state and type the exact confirmation phrase.
actions.2: Submit once and let the page reuse its persisted request ID and expected revision after timeout or reload.
actions.3: Wait for exact convergence before clearing or starting another reset.

reset.guidance: Never invent a new request after an uncertain response. The durable pair prevents duplicate logical resets and unrelated live members must never be touched.

interpretation.title: What readiness does and does not prove
interpretation.purpose: A green fixture proves the server-side synthetic experience is complete and resettable; it does not prove App Store credentials, signed app behavior or the final physical-device walkthrough.

actions.1: Use the page as fixture evidence for release preparation.
actions.2: Track signed-device review login and walkthrough as separate external gates.

interpretation.guidance: Do not turn a green Webadmin status into a claim that provider, purchase or physical-device gates are complete.

admins.title: Admin users help
admins.summary: This owner-controlled allow-list decides which email addresses may request a short-lived Webadmin sign-in code. Active membership is rechecked by Core on every dashboard render and every admin proxy call.

steps.1: Confirm the person's approved operational role and exact email through the owner process.
steps.2: Add or reactivate only that address and verify the role and active state returned by Core.
steps.3: Disable or remove access immediately when authority ends, then confirm the audit event.

addAdmin.title: Add an administrator address
addAdmin.purpose: The form adds one validated email to the Core-owned administrator allow-list under the established default role policy.

actions.1: Enter the exact approved email address.
actions.2: Submit once and verify that the new row appears with the intended state.

addAdmin.guidance: Adding an address grants access to request a login code; it does not send or reveal a permanent password. Confirm authorization outside Webadmin first.

roles.title: Administrator roles
roles.purpose: Rows show owner, admin or viewer role so operators understand whether an account may manage access, perform edits or only read.

actions.1: Review role beside email and activity before changing access state.
actions.2: Use the approved owner process for any role change not offered by this screen.

roles.guidance: The UI does not reconstruct permissions from labels. Core remains authoritative, and AreYouIn or catalog capabilities can add separate bounded ladders.

activeAccess.title: Active state, lock and removal
activeAccess.purpose: Owners can enable or disable membership, clear an active login-code lock, or remove another administrator record.

actions.1: Disable for an immediate reversible access stop.
actions.2: Clear a temporary lock only after understanding why it was triggered.
actions.3: Remove an obsolete administrator after confirming the exact email.

activeAccess.guidance: Revocation is rechecked on every protected request, so an existing browser cookie does not preserve access. Removing a row is stronger than clearing a temporary login lock.

ownerBoundary.title: Owner-only safety boundary
ownerBoundary.purpose: Administrator allow-list mutations are owner-only and self-protection prevents an owner from accidentally disabling or deleting the account currently in use.

actions.1: Use a different approved owner for changes to your own active account.
actions.2: Confirm at least one valid owner path remains before removing another administrator.

ownerBoundary.guidance: A missing or disabled control is intentional protection. Do not bypass it through a lower-level Core call.

audit.title: Audit log help
audit.summary: The Audit log is the chronological, server-authored record of administrative mutations and sensitive operations. It identifies who acted, what operation ran, which target was involved and a deliberately safe subset of details.

steps.1: Refresh before investigating a recent change and start from the newest page.
steps.2: Match actor, action, target and timestamp to the operational event in question.
steps.3: Read safe details and withheld counts without expecting raw payloads or secrets.

navigation.title: Refresh and pagination
navigation.purpose: The page loads a bounded newest-first timeline and lets operators refresh or move through older server pages.

actions.1: Refresh after an expected operation to request the authoritative latest rows.
actions.2: Use Previous and Next to inspect older chronology without altering audit data.

navigation.guidance: The audit log is immutable from this screen and intentionally has no arbitrary browser-side query or delete control.

eventRows.title: Actor, action, target and time
eventRows.purpose: Each row anchors an administrative event to the authenticated email, stable action name, bounded target and server timestamp.

actions.1: Use the four fields together to distinguish similar repeated operations.
actions.2: Compare the event with the affected page's refreshed state or dedicated history.

eventRows.guidance: An audit row proves that Core recorded the operation, not that an external provider or client completed every downstream effect.

safeDetails.title: Safe detail projection
safeDetails.purpose: Only explicitly allow-listed scalar fields are rendered; nested, unknown, empty or overlong material is withheld and counted rather than exposed.

actions.1: Read the visible key-value pairs as bounded context.
actions.2: Note the withheld count when escalating through an authorized server-side investigation.

safeDetails.guidance: Withheld does not mean missing evidence. It protects secrets, private data and unbounded payloads from entering the browser or screenshots.

datesIntakeQueue.title: Intake queue help
datesIntakeQueue.summary: This queue lists the sources handed to the event AI and the drafts it made. A reviewer takes an intake, compares the draft with the source and then rejects it or publishes its events; nothing in the queue is visible to members.

steps.1: Filter by status; intakes in review are ordered with the soonest event first.
steps.2: Take an intake so that no other reviewer works on it at the same time, then open it.
steps.3: Let go of an intake you will not finish, so that it does not wait for your hold to run out.

draftFromSource.title: Draft from source
draftFromSource.purpose: A link, a flyer photo or a line of text is handed to the event AI, which drafts an event sheet for a person to review.
draftFromSource.guidance: The entry is offered only to administrators and only while the draft switch is on. The AI never publishes, and a flyer is never shown publicly.

actions.1: Prefer the organizer's or the venue's own page; pages behind a login cannot be read.
actions.2: After an unanswered request send the same source again while the panel is open; after a reload, look in the queue before you submit it again.

queue.title: Queue, filters and findings
queue.purpose: Each row shows where an intake came from, where it stands, how many events the AI found and what Core's checks flagged.
queue.guidance: A row that cannot be read is named instead of hidden, and a read error is never evidence of an empty queue.

actions.1: Read the blocking problems and warnings before opening a draft.
actions.2: Refresh after another reviewer acts; counts beside the statuses cover the whole queue.

holds.title: Taking and releasing
holds.purpose: A hold reserves an intake for one reviewer for five minutes and is renewed while its page is open.
holds.guidance: Nobody can take an intake from a reviewer whose time has not run out; only a superadmin can release another reviewer's hold.

actions.1: Take an intake only when you are about to review it.
actions.2: Release it when you stop, instead of leaving it to expire.

researchBatch.title: Review a research run together
researchBatch.purpose: A research-run filter narrows the queue to one discovery run and offers batch publication or rejection of its reviewed intakes.
researchBatch.guidance: Only intakes in review with your active hold can be selected. Each intake gets its own result; one refusal does not undo the others.

actions.1: Open and verify each intake, take its hold, then select it in the filtered queue.
actions.2: Confirm the four publication checks once for the selection and write an internal reason, or choose a rejection reason.

datesIntakeDetail.title: Intake review help
datesIntakeDetail.summary: This page shows one intake: what was submitted, what the AI read from it with the evidence for each field, what Core's deterministic checks say, and the actions a reviewer has. The content is an AI draft until a person publishes it through the event editor.

steps.1: Read the status and take the intake; while the pipeline is still working the page checks again by itself.
steps.2: Compare each field with its quote and with the source itself, and read the blocking problems and warnings.
steps.3: Open an event in the editor, correct it, tick the four confirmations and publish - or reject the intake with a reason.

status.title: Status, hold and retention
status.purpose: The status says where the intake stands and why it stopped, who decided, and how long its flyers, texts and record are kept.
status.guidance: Failed, duplicate, expired and waiting-for-budget intakes explain themselves; none of them published anything.

actions.1: Take the intake before deciding; rejecting and publishing need your hold.
actions.2: Use Refresh after a lost answer instead of repeating an action blindly.

inputs.title: Submitted source and flyers
inputs.purpose: The link, the text and the flyers that were submitted, plus the text Core holds of them and checks every quote against.
inputs.guidance: A flyer is private evidence: it is fetched only on request through the console, each view is recorded, and it is never an event image.

actions.1: Open the source link in a new tab and read the event there yourself.
actions.2: Show a flyer only when you need it for the comparison.

evidence.title: AI draft and evidence per field
evidence.purpose: For every field the page shows the AI's claim, the words it quoted and whether Core found those words in the source.
evidence.guidance: Verified means the source says so, not that the source is right. An unverified field is the AI's claim alone and needs your own check.

actions.1: Treat every unverified field and every warning as something to check by hand.
actions.2: Compare the resolved venue and the duplicate candidates before publishing.

editor.title: Editor and publication
editor.purpose: Open in editor prefills the usual external-event form with Core's draft; publication goes through the same publisher and confirmations as a manual event.
editor.guidance: The four confirmations are always yours, an empty field is one Core could not determine, and the event is marked as AI-assisted for members.

actions.1: Publish the events of a multi-event intake one at a time, and say when one is the last.
actions.2: After an unanswered publication retry the saved request; never publish the event again.

reject.title: Rejection
reject.purpose: A rejection ends the intake with one of nine reasons; the statement of reasons is Core's fixed wording for that reason.
reject.guidance: The audit note is required and internal. An intake from which an event was already published can no longer be rejected.

actions.1: Choose the reason that the submitter should be told.
actions.2: Write the audit note so that another reviewer understands the decision.

datesResearch.title: Event research help
datesResearch.summary: Research configures automatic event discovery by city and collection source, shows counts and measured costs, and records each run's candidates. Core owns city geometry, safety checks and scheduling; the console never requests individual member locations.

steps.1: Review the global defaults and budget before enabling automatic research for any city or source.
steps.2: Select a city through search, choose its mode and override only the fields that need a local value.
steps.3: Add a public collection URL, use Test to inspect its candidates, and review imported intakes before publication.

defaults.title: Defaults, switches and budget
defaults.purpose: Global values are inherited by cities; the master and automatic-city switches govern whether scheduled research can start.
defaults.guidance: Limits come from Core. A cost estimate marked not measured yet is unknown, not zero, and never grants additional spending authority.

actions.1: Read the field's effective value and cost guidance before changing the defaults.
actions.2: Compare spend and reservations with the shared event-AI budget, then save with an internal reason.

cities.title: Cities and inherited values
cities.purpose: Each city shows its member count, operating state and reason, effective values, event stock and scheduled research times.
cities.guidance: Core resolves the city's identity and map geometry. Switching miles and kilometres changes display only; always-on mode still obeys safety and budget gates.

actions.1: Choose a city through search; set city bounds or a radius in the research fields.
actions.2: Keep Use global value checked unless the city genuinely needs its own setting.

sources.title: Collection sources and checks
sources.purpose: A source has a public collection URL, city, type, interval and maximum upcoming stock, with its robots state and latest result.
sources.guidance: Test is a dry run and imports nothing. Aggregators provide facts, not copied descriptions; official sources may pass Core's automatic-publication checks.

actions.1: Use a public organiser, venue or city page where possible and choose the correct source type.
actions.2: Run Test to inspect the candidates before using Review now for a real import.

runs.title: Run history and candidates
runs.purpose: History shows found, imported, duplicate and dropped counts with reasons and measured cost, filtered by source, city and run type.
runs.guidance: Queued and running details refresh automatically. An unreadable row is marked unavailable without hiding the remaining history.

actions.1: Open a run to inspect candidate outcomes and the reason each dropped candidate was excluded.
actions.2: For a real import, open its filtered intake queue and review each draft's evidence.

commands.title: Saving, conflicts and safe retries
commands.purpose: Every save is revision-fenced and audited; a logical command keeps one immutable request and idempotency key until its outcome is known.
commands.guidance: For an unknown outcome, use Retry while the page remains open. A revision conflict reloads stored values while preserving your unsaved edits.

actions.1: Explain the change with an internal reason that another administrator can understand.
actions.2: Do not reload an unanswered command to start it again; use the same-command retry offered by the console.

datesAiUsage.title: AI usage help
datesAiUsage.summary: This page shows what the event AI has cost in a calendar month against the monthly cap an administrator set, broken down by provider, model, task and channel. It holds usage figures only: no source, no prompt and no extracted content.

steps.1: Read the spend against the cap and whether the 80% alert or the exhausted state is shown.
steps.2: Check how many intakes wait for budget before deciding whether to raise the cap in Configuration.
steps.3: Use the breakdown to see which provider, model and task the spend comes from.

budget.title: Monthly budget and alerts
budget.purpose: The spend, what is reserved for calls in flight and what remains of the cap, with the alert at 80% and the exhausted state.
budget.guidance: A cap of 0 switches the AI off. When the cap is used up no AI call is made and new intakes wait; the worker retries them every hour.

actions.1: Raise the cap in Configuration when intakes are waiting and the spend is expected.
actions.2: Compare the figure with the provider's invoice; it is computed from list prices.

breakdown.title: Breakdown by provider, model, task and channel
breakdown.purpose: Calls, tokens and cost per provider, model, task and channel, with the model that actually answered.
breakdown.guidance: Unanswered calls and calls with an estimated cost are shown separately, so that a provider outage is visible in the figures.

actions.1: Look at earlier months to compare the cost of a change of model.
actions.2: Treat many unanswered calls as a sign to check the provider order and keys.

pinger.title: Pinger
pinger.subtitle: Configure the server-authoritative interest signal, its artwork and every member-facing message.

overview.title: Hey availability
overview.copy: Members can send a Hey only while both this page's switch and the product-wide Hey switch on Configuration are on. The state below reads the saved settings, not unsaved edits.
overview.boundary: This is configuration eligibility only. A member can still be refused by the pair cooldown or by the daily Hey allowance of their membership plan, and Footprints and photo likes have switches of their own.

states.off: Off on this page. Members cannot send a Hey.
states.globalOff: On here, but the product-wide Hey switch on Configuration is off, so members cannot send a Hey.
states.unknown: On here, but the product-wide Hey switch could not be read. Check Configuration before assuming members can send a Hey.
states.on: On. Members can send a Hey, subject to the pair cooldown and their plan's daily allowance.

overview.globalSettings: Open the feature switches on Configuration
overview.unsaved: You have unsaved changes. Until you save, the state above describes the saved settings.

runtime.title: Runtime policy
runtime.copy: The master switch fails closed. Keep it off until Core, iOS and web have passed the same contract gates.
runtime.actionKeyHelp: Wire identity only. Never rename it when copy changes.
runtime.cooldownHelp: How long one member must wait before sending another Hey to the same person.
runtime.retentionHelp: How long a received Hey stays in the recipient's Heys tab. A change applies to Heys sent after saving.
runtime.chatContractHelp: Enable version 1 only after the chat migration has completed.
runtime.chatContractLocked: Locked until the verified migration and an explicit production release permit are present.
runtime.gateDefault: Default new members to ‘only people I sent a Hey may message me’
runtime.gateDefaultHelp: Applies to every member who has not chosen this setting themselves; a member's own choice always wins.

icon.title: Action icon
icon.copy: Two states, each in both appearances. Upload a PNG or an SVG that Core turns into managed PNG variants.
icon.staged: Icon uploaded. Save the configuration to publish its URL.
icon.useBundledHint: With this on none of the four uploads is needed; anything already uploaded is kept but not used.

copy.title: Administrator-owned copy
copy.copy: English and Hungarian are required. Keep the documented brace placeholders exactly where shown.

keys.cooldown_error: Cooldown error — requires the remaining placeholder
keys.push_body: Push body — requires the sender placeholder
keys.banner_text: In-app banner — requires the sender placeholder

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.empty: No Pinger operations have been recorded yet.

enabled.title: Page switch for Hey
enabled.purpose: The master switch for Hey on this page. It fails closed, so keep it off until Core and the released apps have passed the same contract checks.
enabled.effect: Off makes Core refuse every Hey, whatever the product-wide switch says. On is not enough by itself: the product-wide Hey switch on Configuration must be on as well.
enabled.example: To pause Hey during an incident, switch it off here and save; the overview above then shows Off, and switching it back on restores the same settings.

cooldown.title: Pair cooldown
cooldown.purpose: The minimum wait, in seconds, between two Heys from the same sender to the same recipient. The hint under the field shows the value in days, hours and minutes.
cooldown.effect: A sender who tries again sooner is refused with the cooldown message, which shows the remaining time through its remaining placeholder.
cooldown.example: 86400 seconds reads as 1 day: after a Hey to one person, the sender can send a Hey to someone else at once, but to that same person only a day later.

retention.title: Collector retention
retention.purpose: How long, in seconds, a received Hey stays in the recipient's Heys tab. The hint under the field shows the value in days, hours and minutes.
retention.effect: Each Hey gets its expiry when it is sent, so a new value applies to Heys sent after the save; Heys already received keep the expiry they were given.
retention.example: 604800 seconds reads as 7 days: a Hey sent today disappears from the recipient's Heys tab a week later.

chatDefault.title: Default chat gate for members
chatDefault.purpose: The starting value of the member setting that lets only people the member has sent a Hey to message them.
chatDefault.effect: It applies to every member who has not chosen this setting themselves; a member's own choice always wins, and changing the default never rewrites a stored choice. It matters only at chat contract version 1; at 0 the gate is hidden.
chatDefault.example: Turn it on to protect members from unsolicited first messages by default; anyone who switched the setting off in the app keeps it off.

chatContract.title: Chat contract version
chatContract.purpose: Chooses whether the chat request and gate behaviour tied to Hey is active: 0 keeps the gate hidden, 1 turns requests and the gate on.
chatContract.effect: Version 1 can be chosen only when Core reports that the verified chat migration and the release permit are in place; until then the control stays locked.
chatContract.example: Keep it at 0 during rollout; once the page unlocks version 1, switch to it with a single save.

actionKey.title: Stable action key
actionKey.purpose: The internal identity every stored Hey carries on the wire. It is shown read-only under Technical settings and is not part of the member-facing copy.
actionKey.effect: The app rejects a Heys page whose rows carry a different key, so renaming it would break every member's Heys tab until the old Heys expire.
actionKey.example: Changing the button text is a copy change further down this page; the action key stays ping.

states.title: Resting and sent states
states.purpose: Four icon slots: the Hey button at rest and after the viewer has sent that member a Hey, each in the light and the dark appearance.
states.effect: The app shows the resting icon until the viewer has sent that member a Hey, then the sent icon. An empty slot falls back to the app's bundled artwork.
states.example: Upload the sent-state pair when the button should visibly change after a Hey; leave it empty to keep the bundled sent icon.

upload.title: Uploading icons
upload.purpose: Each slot accepts a PNG or an SVG, which Core turns into managed PNG variants. With “Use the app's bundled icons” on, no upload is needed.
upload.effect: An upload is only staged: its URL is published when you save the configuration. Uploads stay stored while the bundled switch is on, so switching it off brings them back.
upload.example: Upload all four files, check the previews, then save once; switching to the bundled icons later does not delete them.

messages.title: Member-facing messages
messages.purpose: Every text members see around Hey: the button accessibility label, the success toast, the cooldown and generic refusals, the Heys tab title, the push title and body, the in-app banner and the closed chat gate note.
messages.effect: English and Hungarian are both required; the app shows the member's language, and each field has the length limit shown under it.
messages.example: To rename the Heys tab, change its title in both languages and save; the action key and stored Heys are not affected.

placeholders.title: Placeholders in messages
placeholders.purpose: Some messages must keep a placeholder that the app or Core fills in: the cooldown error needs the remaining placeholder, and the push body and the banner need the sender placeholder.
placeholders.effect: A message that loses its required placeholder, or gains an unknown one, fails validation and cannot be saved, so members never see a sentence with a gap.
placeholders.example: Write the cooldown message as a full sentence and keep the remaining placeholder, in braces, exactly as in the current text; only the words around it change.

history.title: Configuration history
history.purpose: The most recent configuration and icon operations, each with the administrator, the revision change and the time; the badge in the header is the current revision.
history.effect: Every save creates a new revision. If another administrator saved first, your save is refused as a conflict and the newer version is loaded for review.
history.example: Before changing the cooldown, check here whether someone changed it recently; the trail records who and when, not why.

errors.load: The Pinger configuration could not be loaded.
errors.save: The Pinger configuration could not be saved.
errors.upload: The icon could not be uploaded.
errors.validation: Fix the highlighted fields before saving.
errors.field: This value does not match the deployed contract.
errors.conflict: Another administrator saved a newer revision. The current server version has been loaded; review your changes before trying again.

login.brandCopy: Manage the Friending community, campaigns and runtime controls from one secure place.
login.securityNote: Restricted to approved administrators. Every operational change is audited.
login.title: Welcome back
login.subtitle: Use an approved email address. We will send a short-lived sign-in code.
login.codeIntro: Enter the 6-digit code sent to {email}. It expires after 10 minutes.
login.privacy: The Core credential and your session signing key never reach the browser.
login.invalid: The code is incorrect. Check it and try again.
login.expired: This code has expired. Request a new one.
login.banned: Too many incorrect attempts. This account is temporarily locked.
login.rateLimited: Too many requests. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
login.requestFailed: The code could not be sent right now. Please try again shortly.
login.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.

overview.title: Overview
overview.subtitle: A live snapshot of the community and the controls that shape discovery.
overview.signupsNote: Real accounts registered in each rolling period. Demo and test accounts are excluded. Persona counts show current successful verification, not administrator exemptions.
overview.signupsUnavailable: Signup metrics are unavailable. Refresh to try again.
overview.quickActionsCopy: Common operational tasks, one click away.
overview.manageUsersCopy: Search profiles and inspect account details.
overview.manageAppearanceCopy: Rules for the app landing screen, the Discover hero carousel and the light/dark palette.
overview.manageConfigCopy: Change allow-listed product controls without a deploy.
overview.recentAuditCopy: The latest administrative changes across Friending.
overview.noAudit: No administrative changes have been recorded yet.
overview.loadError: The operational snapshot could not be loaded.

users.title: Registered users
users.subtitle: Search accounts, distinguish demo profiles and inspect the data needed for support.
users.searchLabel: Name, email, user ID or username
users.resultCount: {count, plural, =0 {No users} one {# user} other {# users}}
users.membershipSummaryNote: Membership facts are resolved by Core for this server-paginated page. Earliest source date may come from Store evidence, an administrator grant, or legacy compatibility; by itself it does not prove a verified Store purchase.
users.demoAccessNote: Special access takes effect while Demo system is enabled in Runtime configuration.
users.permissionSaveError: The demo visibility permission could not be updated.
users.noRowsCopy: Try a broader name search or switch the account-type filter.
users.loadError: Registered users could not be loaded.

filterRefused.phoneCheckInvalid: Core refused the phone filter. Reset the filters and try again.

users.filterIgnored: Core did not confirm the signup platform or phone filter, so this list may not be filtered the way you asked.

membershipConfig.title: Membership plans
membershipConfig.subtitle: Configure the benefits and explicit limits shared by FREE and PLUS members. Store product identities are deployment-owned and cannot be edited here.
membershipConfig.loadError: The membership configuration could not be loaded.
membershipConfig.readyConfirm: Mark this configuration ready for enforcement? Core starts enforcing the plan once this marker and the server's enforcement switch are both on.

dirty.leaveConfirm: Leave this page and discard the unsaved membership-plan changes?

validation.validCopy: Every quota rule matches the current bounds supplied by Core.
validation.invalidCopy: {count} invalid rule(s) block saving. Every problem is listed below.
validation.nonFiniteValue: {quota} · {tier}: disabled and unlimited rules cannot carry a numeric value.
validation.finiteValueInvalid: {quota} · {tier}: enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.

rollout.title: Release gates
rollout.copy: Deployment-owned switches are read-only here. They prevent a saved draft from changing live access before every client and server gate is complete.
rollout.shadowWarning: Feature enforcement is off. Changes can be reviewed and tested, but they do not yet replace the current production restrictions.
rollout.featureDependencyUnknown: Membership V1 does not report the separate Pinger master switch or saved-phrases rollout switch. The limits below do not prove that either feature is live.

benefits.title: Capabilities
benefits.copy: A capability is either available or unavailable for each tier. Core remains the final authority even when a client is stale.

capabilityHelp.invisible_presence: Allows Invisible mode; Core never publishes the member as online while it is selected.
capabilityHelp.hide_profile_visit: Allows the 20-second server lease and an acknowledged hidden visit.
capabilityHelp.vip_badge: Makes the member eligible for the PLUS badge; the member may hide it in Settings.

limits.title: Quotas and resource limits
limits.copy: Every tier is explicit: disabled, finite, or unlimited. Daily counters reset at 00:00 UTC; concurrent limits count active resources.

preview.title: What members receive
preview.copy: This is the member-facing interpretation of the current editor draft. Unsaved values and disabled rollout gates are not live promises.
preview.switchedOff: Switched-off feature — not shown to members
preview.switchStateUnreadable: Feature-switch state unavailable — not shown to members
preview.presetsCopy: Each preset creates audited, time-bounded PLUS access. It does not record a payment or change Store billing.

products.title: Store products
products.copy: This allow-list is compiled into Core. Editing a quota can never authorize an arbitrary billing product.
products.googlePendingCopy: Android billing stays blocked until the Play Console products and server verification authority are provisioned.

readiness.title: Configuration readiness
readiness.copy: Use this marker only after the values, copy, migrations and compatibility matrix have been reviewed.
readiness.label: This revision is ready for enforcement
readiness.hint: Enforcement starts only when this marker and the server's enforcement switch are both on.
readiness.ownerOnly: Only an owner can change the readiness marker; administrators can still edit plan benefits and limits.

liveLock.title: This plan is marked ready for enforcement. Only an owner can change it.
liveLock.copy: Once the server's enforcement switch is on, every change to this plan reaches all members at once, so Core accepts changes to it only from an owner. The editor and Save stay read-only for your role; ask an owner to make the change.

membershipErrors.configurationConflictAdopted: Another operator saved a newer membership configuration. Its authoritative version replaced this draft; review it before editing again.
membershipErrors.grantConflict: This member's PLUS grant changed meanwhile. Review the latest membership state, preview again, and then retry.
membershipErrors.grantIdInvalid: The console sent an invalid grant identifier. This is a technical error; reload the page and report it if it happens again.

membershipErrors.revokeConflict: The administrator grant changed before revocation completed. Review the latest authoritative state before retrying.
membershipErrors.requestConflict: This operation identifier was already used for a different membership change. Start the action again from the current authoritative state.
membershipErrors.expiryInvalid: The expiry must be a valid future UTC instant after the grant start.
membershipErrors.horizonExceeded: Administrator access cannot extend more than 730 days from the current server time.
membershipErrors.ownerRequired: Only an owner can perform this membership action.
membershipErrors.writeRequired: This administrator role is read-only for membership changes.
membershipErrors.accessRevoked: This administrator account has been revoked and cannot change membership state.

grant.title: Issue or extend PLUS access
grant.copy: This creates an audited, time-bounded admin source. It never records a payment or changes Apple/Google evidence.
grant.startNowWarning: Start now may overlap verified Store access. It never pauses, cancels, or extends Apple or Google billing.
grant.overlapWarning: This grant overlaps active Store access. The Store subscription keeps billing and running independently.
grant.overlapConfirm: This Start now grant overlaps active Store access and will not pause Store billing. Issue the overlapping grant?
grant.discardConfirm: Discard the pending grant request? The member is read again first. If their administrator grant is still unchanged, the request is dropped even though its outcome is unknown; if Core applies it later anyway, a new grant issued now would add access a second time.
grant.discarded: The pending request was discarded. The member's administrator grant was unchanged when checked; refresh before issuing another grant.
grant.discardUnreadable: The member could not be read, so the pending request was kept and stays locked. Try again when Core answers.
grant.uncertainResolved: The member's administrator grant changed after a request whose outcome was unknown, so that request most likely went through. Check the refreshed state before issuing another grant.
grant.previewStale: The member's administrator grant changed since this preview, or could not be read to confirm it. Nothing was sent: check the refreshed state and preview the grant again.
grant.pendingCopy: A grant request sent earlier still has no confirmed outcome. Its settings are shown above and stay locked. Resending sends exactly the same request, so it cannot add access twice; discarding first reads the member again and compares their grant with the one the request was based on.
grant.restoreExpired: A grant request with an unknown outcome was pinned more than {minutes} minutes ago, so it was not restored after the reload. Refresh and check the member's administrator grant and history before issuing another grant.
grant.extendAutoRenewWarning: This member's store subscription renews automatically. With “Extend effective access” the grant starts when the current store period ends, so while renewals succeed it runs alongside paid time and adds nothing; it only matters if the member cancels or a renewal fails. Use “Start now” to compensate right away.

personaAdmin.subtitle: Manage guarded member verification overrides and design the copy of the three verification screens the app shows around Persona.

readiness.title: Contract readiness
readiness.copy: Core is the authority for schema version, release readiness and every available action.
readiness.contractLocked: Core has not released receipt-backed Persona mutations. Navigation, proxy actions and every production control remain closed.
readiness.readyCopy: The released contract is active, but each visible control still follows the exact action list returned for this administrator.

receipts.pendingCopy: The exact {action} request for {target} is retained in this browser session. Competing Persona changes stay locked until its result is resolved.
receipts.sending: The durable request identity was saved before sending. Waiting for Core's canonical receipt.
receipts.converged: An authoritative configuration read proved that the retained save converged. Its stored request identity was cleared.
receipts.replayed: Core replayed the canonical completed receipt; no second logical mutation was created.
receipts.conflict: The expected revision is stale. The retained request was cleared; refresh authoritative state before creating a new request.
receipts.uncertain: The response was lost, malformed, or outside the closed receipt contract. The exact request remains stored; retry that request only.
receipts.persistenceUnavailable: Session receipt storage is unavailable or contains an invalid pending row. Persona mutations remain locked so an uncertain request identity cannot be lost.
receipts.persistenceCleanupFailed: Core returned a valid result, but the stored request identity could not be cleared. Controls remain locked; retrying will reuse the same receipt.

apply_fake.title: Apply synthetic marker
apply_fake.copy: Marks an otherwise unverified member with an explicitly synthetic, admin-applied Persona state. It is not a provider identity check and does not verify the phone.

revoke_fake.title: Revoke synthetic marker
revoke_fake.copy: Removes only the guarded admin-applied marker. Core refuses provider-backed and force-promoted verification states.

force_verify.title: Promote current avatar
force_verify.copy: Copies the member's current durable avatar into accepted Persona verification evidence. This is a high-impact operator override.

confirm.apply_fake: Apply an explicitly synthetic admin marker to {name} (UID {uid})? This does not represent a Persona provider check and does not change phone verification.
confirm.revoke_fake: Remove the synthetic Persona marker from {name} (UID {uid})? Core will refuse this if the current state is provider-backed or force-promoted.
confirm.force_verify: Promote the current avatar of {name} (UID {uid}) into accepted verification evidence? This replaces that member's Persona verification image and cannot be undone from this screen.

success.apply_fake: Core returned the canonical synthetic-marker receipt. A new marker advances the shared revision once; an already-present marker keeps its revision.
success.revoke_fake: Core removed the guarded synthetic marker and advanced the shared member revision exactly once.
success.force_verify: Core promoted the current avatar, advanced the shared member revision, and returned a valid bounded path that was not retained in browser state.

screens.title: Verification screens the app shows
screens.copy: The pre-verification, success and failed screens members see around Persona. The nine headline, subtitle and primary-button fields use the app's own compiled copy when empty. The optional PRE link is different: it has no compiled default, so an empty label or URL means no link button.
screens.loadError: The Persona screens console could not be decoded safely. Nothing editable has been assumed.
screens.readOnly: Your role may read this copy but not change it. Core decides that, and this console cannot widen it.
