Everything else keeps working: the AreYouIn worker still delivers notifications, ends expired activities and runs scheduled purges, and logs a warning. Save an approved number of days below to allow live sharing.
configuration.storefrontOverridesHelp: Map uppercase three-letter storefront codes to true or false. Use an empty object to inherit the global switch everywhere. Core validates the supported country codes; this never enables the AreYouIn section itself.

runtimeHelp.title: Runtime settings help
runtimeHelp.intro: This guide describes the Core-owned behavior behind every AreYouIn runtime setting. It shows the value currently returned by Core, the stored value, the safe default and the validation bounds. Saving a value is immediate for new requests, but it does not migrate existing records or start background infrastructure.
runtimeHelp.beforeChangingCopy: Treat feature switches, retention rules and workers as one release unit. Use this order when enabling AreYouIn or a high-impact capability:
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepRetention: Approve the privacy and legal retention values, especially live trails and moderation evidence.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepWorker: Deploy and verify the AreYouIn background worker, monitoring and delivery dependencies.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepMaster: In Configuration, set AreYouIn availability for the controlled storefronts and verify the client bootstrap and entry point.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepCapabilities: Enable creation, live sharing, reviews and digest separately; do not switch them all on at once.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepVerify: Watch errors, moderation queues, worker lag and audit logs before widening rollout.
runtimeHelp.effectiveNote: AreYouIn section availability is edited in Configuration, not on this page. A subordinate effective value can still be OFF while its stored value is ON. The effective value is the global answer: what members get where their storefront has no AreYouIn override. Where a storefront has its own availability, each rollout switch also shows its value in that storefront, and that is what members there get.
runtimeHelp.timingNote: Durations and retention values are usually copied into a record when an activity, decline, case or purge schedule is created. Changing the default does not rewrite existing deadlines unless a dedicated migration or operation does so.
runtimeHelp.liveRetentionUnset: Not set, so live sharing is off. The AreYouIn worker keeps running and logs a warning; notifications, expiry and scheduled purges are unaffected.
runtimeHelp.unknownCopy: Core returned settings that are not part of this Webadmin release's bounded help catalog.
runtimeHelp.unknownSettingCopy: Do not change this setting until the matching Core release notes and operating procedure have been reviewed.

rollout.title: Feature rollout switches
rollout.copy: Independent AreYouIn capability controls. Section availability itself is managed once in Configuration. OFF preserves data; it does not delete anything.

activityLifecycle.title: Activity lifecycle and limits
activityLifecycle.copy: Defaults and deadlines used when activities, memberships and capacity rules are created or reconciled.

rateLimits.title: Abuse and load limits
rateLimits.copy: Server-enforced per-actor limits. A rejected request returns a rate-limit error; lowering a value never removes already accepted data.

safetyRetention.title: Safety, moderation and retention
safetyRetention.copy: High-impact operational and privacy settings. Agree retention and escalation policy before changing these values.

digest.title: Nearby digest defaults
digest.copy: Background nearby-suggestion scheduling. User opt-in, eligibility, timezone and personal quiet-hour preferences still apply.

externalEvents.title: External events
externalEvents.copy: Manual external-event availability, participant invitation limits and the entry window. These controls do not enable AI, automatic publication or research.

eventIntake.title: AI event intake (Draft from source)
eventIntake.copy: The switch, the budget, the providers and their models for the AI that drafts external events from a link, a flyer or a line of text. Nothing here takes effect while the draft switch is off, and the AI never publishes: a person reviews every draft.

eventSuggestion.title: Members' event suggestions
eventSuggestion.copy: The switch, the limits, the strike rule and the consent version of the channel through which members suggest public events. A suggestion is drafted by the same AI and reviewed by a person; nothing here takes effect while the suggestion switch is off.

dates_external_events_enabled.title: External events
dates_external_events_enabled.purpose: Controls external-event availability within AreYouIn; the stored default is ON.
dates_external_events_enabled.effect: The effective result also requires AreYouIn availability in the member's storefront and a compatible client request. Core returns the global result and storefront-specific results.
dates_external_events_enabled.caution: This is not the AreYouIn section switch and does not enable older clients. Turning it off preserves event records.

dates_external_events_enabled_overrides.title: External events by storefront
dates_external_events_enabled_overrides.purpose: Overrides the external-event switch for individual uppercase three-letter storefront codes.
dates_external_events_enabled_overrides.effect: A missing code inherits the external-event global switch; an empty map removes all overrides. A true value cannot override a disabled AreYouIn section.
dates_external_events_enabled_overrides.caution: Values must be JSON booleans, not strings. Check the effective result on the external-event switch row; do not treat the stored override as proof of availability.

dates_external_publishing_enabled.title: External-event publication rollout
dates_external_publishing_enabled.purpose: Separate publication and content-correction switch. Its default is OFF; only the exact stored boolean true enables new writes.
dates_external_publishing_enabled.effect: OFF refuses publication and corrections without creating artifacts. Previous successful receipts can still be replayed, and safety commands such as cancellation and withdrawal stay available.
dates_external_publishing_enabled.caution: The release lead enables this only after compatible Core and Webadmin P1 are both live. This is independent of member/storefront visibility and is never enabled by deployment or schema installation.

dates_event_invite_daily_limit.title: External-event invitations per day
dates_event_invite_daily_limit.purpose: Sets the daily invitation ceiling for each member inviting others to external events.
dates_event_invite_daily_limit.effect: The default is 20; Core accepts whole numbers from 1 to 1000. Event eligibility and recipient privacy checks remain separate requirements.
dates_event_invite_daily_limit.caution: This is separate from member-hosted activity invitation limits. Raising it does not bypass blocks, cooldowns or client compatibility.

dates_event_invite_per_event_limit.title: External-event invitations per inviter and event
dates_event_invite_per_event_limit.purpose: Caps the invitations one member may send for the same external event.
dates_event_invite_per_event_limit.effect: The default is 10; Core accepts whole numbers from 1 to 1000. The daily ceiling applies as well.
dates_event_invite_per_event_limit.caution: A larger limit does not make an ineligible recipient invitable or create repeated pending invitations.

dates_event_lookahead_days.title: Manual event entry window
dates_event_lookahead_days.purpose: Limits how far into the future a manually entered external event may start.
dates_event_lookahead_days.effect: The default is 180 days; Core accepts whole numbers from 1 to 730 and checks the event time inside the receipted command.
dates_event_lookahead_days.caution: This is not the event duration or an AI research schedule. Existing successful retries keep their original receipt.

dates_creation_enabled.title: Activity creation
dates_creation_enabled.purpose: Controls creation drafts and publishing of new AreYouIn activities, including whether the app advertises the creation capability.
dates_creation_enabled.effect: ON permits eligible users to create and publish subject to validation, moderation and rate limits. OFF blocks the new-activity flow; existing activity data and allowed management operations remain available.
dates_creation_enabled.caution: AreYouIn section availability is managed in Configuration. Disable creation first when stopping new supply while keeping existing activities operational.

dates_live_sharing_enabled.title: Host live-location sharing
dates_live_sharing_enabled.purpose: Controls the host's live session, pause/resume state and ingestion of bounded location trail points for an active activity.
dates_live_sharing_enabled.effect: ON permits live operations only when a positive live-trail retention is configured. OFF denies live session and point operations and exposes the capability as unavailable.
dates_live_sharing_enabled.caution: This handles highly sensitive location data. Set and approve dates_live_trail_retention_days, deploy the AreYouIn worker and verify purge monitoring before enabling it.

dates_reviews_enabled.title: Post-activity reviews
dates_reviews_enabled.purpose: Controls participant review and host check-in capabilities after an activity ends, plus visibility of AreYouIn review surfaces.
dates_reviews_enabled.effect: ON lets eligible participants submit/view the supported review flow. OFF fails review operations closed and removes the capability from the app; stored reviews and moderation history are not deleted.
dates_reviews_enabled.caution: Review moderation and evidence retention remain separate safety concerns. AreYouIn section availability is managed in Configuration.

dates_digest_enabled.title: Nearby activity digest
dates_digest_enabled.purpose: Controls the background job that evaluates opted-in users and queues grouped nearby-activity suggestion notifications.
dates_digest_enabled.effect: ON lets the worker process eligible users according to frequency, quiet hours, origin and personal preferences. OFF makes digest batches exit without producing new digest events.
dates_digest_enabled.caution: This does not disable ordinary activity, reminder or moderation notifications. A running AreYouIn worker and notification delivery path are required.

dates_default_scheduled_duration_minutes.title: Default scheduled duration
dates_default_scheduled_duration_minutes.purpose: The suggested activity length sent to clients when they build a new scheduled activity.
dates_default_scheduled_duration_minutes.effect: A larger value proposes a later end time; a smaller value proposes a shorter activity. It is a creation default, not the maximum duration enforced on every activity.
dates_default_scheduled_duration_minutes.caution: Existing drafts and activities are not rewritten. Clients normally pick up the new default after refreshing their AreYouIn bootstrap.

dates_tbd_expiry_days.title: TBD activity lifetime
dates_tbd_expiry_days.purpose: Sets the automatic expiry deadline assigned to a newly created activity whose time is still to be decided.
dates_tbd_expiry_days.effect: After this many days the worker ends an unresolved TBD activity, invalidates pending membership states and makes its chat read-only. Longer values leave undecided activities discoverable longer.
dates_tbd_expiry_days.caution: The deadline is stored on creation and is not retroactively recalculated for existing TBD activities. Automatic expiry requires the AreYouIn worker.

dates_now_lifetime_hours.title: Now activity lifetime
dates_now_lifetime_hours.purpose: Sets the automatic end deadline assigned when a new immediate, “Now” activity is created.
dates_now_lifetime_hours.effect: The worker ends the activity at its stored deadline, closes live sharing, invalidates pending membership states and makes chat read-only. A longer lifetime keeps immediate activities active longer.
dates_now_lifetime_hours.caution: Existing Now activities keep their stored auto-end time. This value does not replace manual host/admin end or cancel operations.

dates_now_warning_minutes.title: Now auto-close warning
dates_now_warning_minutes.purpose: Defines how far before a Now activity's auto-end deadline the system queues its one-time closing-soon warning.
dates_now_warning_minutes.effect: A larger value warns earlier; a smaller value warns closer to auto-close. The worker evaluates active activities against the current warning window.
dates_now_warning_minutes.caution: This changes notification timing only; it does not extend the activity lifetime. Worker cadence can affect the exact delivery minute.

dates_decline_cooldown_hours.title: Declined request cooldown
dates_decline_cooldown_hours.purpose: Prevents a user from immediately sending another join request after the host declines that user's request for the same activity.
dates_decline_cooldown_hours.effect: A decline writes a cooldown deadline using this value. Until that deadline, another join/request attempt is rejected. Larger values reduce repeat requests but also delay legitimate retries.
dates_decline_cooldown_hours.caution: Changing the setting affects cooldowns written by future declines; it does not rewrite an already stored cooldown_until value.

dates_reinvite_cooldown_hours.title: Re-invite cooldown after a declined invitation
dates_reinvite_cooldown_hours.purpose: Stops a host from inviting a member to the same activity again right after the member declined the invitation.
dates_reinvite_cooldown_hours.effect: For this many hours after the member's decline, Core refuses another invite of that member to that activity with dates-invite-cooldown and leaves the member out of the host's invite candidates. A join request the host declined starts no invite cooldown.
dates_reinvite_cooldown_hours.caution: The cooldown is measured from the stored decline time, so a change applies at once to existing declines too. An invite to a member who muted the host is refused whatever this value is.

dates_invalidated_visibility_hours.title: Invalidated membership visibility
dates_invalidated_visibility_hours.purpose: Defines the short grace period during which an invitation or request invalidated by an activity ending, expiring or being canceled remains visible as historical state.
dates_invalidated_visibility_hours.effect: A larger value keeps the terminal state visible longer; a smaller value hides it sooner after invalidation. It supports understandable UI transitions without keeping it active.
dates_invalidated_visibility_hours.caution: This is a visibility deadline, not the retention policy for activity, chat, audit or moderation data. Existing stored deadlines are not globally rewritten.

dates_maximum_headcount_limit.title: Maximum selectable headcount
dates_maximum_headcount_limit.purpose: Caps the maximum_people value a host may choose for capacity-limited auto-join activities; the count includes the host.
dates_maximum_headcount_limit.effect: New or edited capacity values must be at least 2, no lower than the current going count and no higher than this limit. Approval-mode activities do not use this capacity field.
dates_maximum_headcount_limit.caution: Lowering the cap does not remove participants or automatically shrink existing activities, but a later edit must satisfy current validation.

dates_creation_rate_limit.title: Activity publish limit
dates_creation_rate_limit.purpose: Limits how many successfully published AreYouIn activities one user can create in the preceding 24 hours.
dates_creation_rate_limit.effect: When the completed publish count reaches the limit, further publishes return a rate-limit error until earlier publishes leave the window. Draft editing is not itself a successful publish.
dates_creation_rate_limit.caution: Lowering the value does not unpublish activities. Set it high enough for legitimate hosts but low enough to contain spam and moderation load.

dates_request_rate_limit.title: Join-request attempt limit
dates_request_rate_limit.purpose: Limits repeated approval-mode join requests by one user for the same activity inside a 24-hour attempt window.
dates_request_rate_limit.effect: Each accepted request attempt increments the membership's request window counter. At the limit, another attempt is rejected until that window resets.
dates_request_rate_limit.caution: This works alongside the decline cooldown; it does not cap total requests received by a host across different users.

dates_rejoin_rate_limit.title: Rejoin attempt limit
dates_rejoin_rate_limit.purpose: Limits how often a user who left an auto-join activity can rejoin that same activity inside a 24-hour attempt window.
dates_rejoin_rate_limit.effect: The first join is not a rejoin. Subsequent left-to-joined transitions increment the per-membership rejoin counter and are rejected once the limit is reached.
dates_rejoin_rate_limit.caution: This protects membership and notification churn. It does not change host invitations, approval decisions or joins to other activities.

dates_invite_daily_limit.title: Host invite limit per day
dates_invite_daily_limit.purpose: Limits how many invitations one host can send across all of their activities in a rolling 24 hours.
dates_invite_daily_limit.effect: Every completed invite counts. At the limit, Core refuses the next invite with dates-invite-rate-limited until the oldest invite in the window is more than 24 hours old.
dates_invite_daily_limit.caution: Too low a value stops a host from inviting a whole group at once; too high a value lets one host send invitations, and their pushes, to many strangers. It does not limit join requests or approvals.

dates_invite_activity_daily_limit.title: Invite limit per activity per day
dates_invite_activity_daily_limit.purpose: Limits how many invitations a host can send for one activity in a rolling 24 hours.
dates_invite_activity_daily_limit.effect: Counted separately from the host's daily total. Whichever limit is reached first refuses the next invite with dates-invite-rate-limited.
dates_invite_activity_daily_limit.caution: Keep it at or below the host's daily limit: a higher value has no effect, because the daily total is reached first.

dates_chat_message_rate_limit.title: Chat messages per minute
dates_chat_message_rate_limit.purpose: Caps messages sent by one user to one AreYouIn thread during the preceding 60 seconds, including supported update/pin messages.
dates_chat_message_rate_limit.effect: At the limit, another message to that thread returns a rate-limit error. Different senders and threads have independent counts.
dates_chat_message_rate_limit.caution: Raising this increases write, notification and abuse load. Lowering it does not delete or delay messages already accepted.

dates_live_point_rate_limit.title: Live location points per minute
dates_live_point_rate_limit.purpose: Caps newly accepted live-location trail points from one host across the preceding 60 seconds.
dates_live_point_rate_limit.effect: A batch is rejected when its new points plus the host's recent accepted points exceed the limit. Idempotent duplicate points do not consume the new-point count again.
dates_live_point_rate_limit.caution: Balance route quality against sensitive-data volume and write load. This setting matters only when live sharing and positive trail retention are both active.

dates_report_sla_hours.title: Report moderation SLA
dates_report_sla_hours.purpose: Sets the due-time target attached to new user-submitted AreYouIn reports and their active moderation case.
dates_report_sla_hours.effect: The due timestamp is report creation time plus this many hours; a case keeps the earliest due time across attached reports. Queue SLA metrics and breach indicators use that timestamp.
dates_report_sla_hours.caution: Changing the value does not recalculate existing case deadlines, and it does not change the separate prepublication review deadline.

dates_distinct_report_suspend_threshold.title: Distinct-reporter escalation threshold
dates_distinct_report_suspend_threshold.purpose: Marks a report case as escalated when reports reach this number of unique reporter accounts.
dates_distinct_report_suspend_threshold.effect: At or above the threshold Core sets escalated=true so the case is more visible to moderators. Duplicate reports from the same reporter do not increase the distinct count.
dates_distinct_report_suspend_threshold.caution: Despite the historical key name, this does not automatically suspend an account or remove content. Restriction or suspension always requires an authorized moderation decision.

dates_activity_soft_delete_retention_day.title: Soft-deleted activity retention
dates_activity_soft_delete_retention_day.purpose: Sets the earliest hard-purge eligibility date when an administrator soft-deletes an AreYouIn activity.
dates_activity_soft_delete_retention_day.effect: Soft delete immediately removes the activity from normal operation and writes purge_eligible_at for this many days later. Actual hard purge remains a separate authorized operation.
dates_activity_soft_delete_retention_day.caution: Changing the default does not reschedule already soft-deleted activities. Legal, audit, moderation and related-record constraints may require longer preservation.

dates_live_trail_retention_days.title: Live trail retention
dates_live_trail_retention_days.purpose: Defines how long terminated live-location sessions and point trails remain before worker-driven purge.
dates_live_trail_retention_days.effect: A positive day count allows live sharing and schedules the trail purge when an activity ends, is canceled or deleted. While it is empty, Core refuses live sharing, even with the live-sharing switch on; the AreYouIn worker keeps running (notifications, expiry and scheduled purges continue) and logs a warning.
dates_live_trail_retention_days.caution: This is a privacy-critical prerequisite for live sharing. Approve the period, run the AreYouIn worker and monitor purge lag before turning live sharing ON; case evidence copied under authorization has its own policy.

moderation_evidence_retention_days.title: Moderation evidence retention
moderation_evidence_retention_days.purpose: Defines the post-hold retention period for restricted evidence snapshots stored with AreYouIn moderation cases.
moderation_evidence_retention_days.effect: When an automatic or legal hold is closed, a positive value schedules evidence purge this many days later. An empty value does not create a new automatic purge deadline.
moderation_evidence_retention_days.caution: An active legal hold takes precedence. This setting does not purge case decisions or audit history and should be approved with privacy/legal owners before use.

dates_digest_frequency.title: Digest frequency
dates_digest_frequency.purpose: Selects the normal interval used by the AreYouIn worker when rescheduling eligible nearby-activity digest evaluation.
dates_digest_frequency.effect: daily uses a one-day interval; weekly uses a seven-day interval. A digest is queued only when the user is eligible, opted in and has new joinable nearby activities.
dates_digest_frequency.caution: This is not a promise of an exact delivery time. Existing next-run timestamps, quiet hours, worker cadence and notification delivery can defer processing.

dates_digest_quiet_hours.title: Default digest quiet hours
dates_digest_quiet_hours.purpose: Provides the default local-time quiet-hour start and end advertised for AreYouIn notification settings.
dates_digest_quiet_hours.effect: When quiet hours are enabled for a user, scheduled digest delivery is deferred while the user's local clock is inside this interval. A range such as 22:00–08:00 crosses midnight.
dates_digest_quiet_hours.caution: This is a default, not a mandatory global blackout. Existing explicit user preferences remain authoritative, and the user's timezone is used with UTC as a safe fallback.

dates_external_admin_drafts_enabled.title: Draft from source
dates_external_admin_drafts_enabled.purpose: Master switch of the AI event intake for administrators. Its default is OFF; only the exact stored boolean true turns it on.
dates_external_admin_drafts_enabled.effect: OFF refuses creating an intake and publishing from one, stores nothing and leaves the intake worker with nothing to do, so no AI spend can occur. Intakes already in the queue can still be read and rejected.
dates_external_admin_drafts_enabled.caution: Turn it on only after the AI provider keys are installed on the server and the monthly budget is set. It is independent of the external-event publication switch, which publishing a draft also needs.

dates_ai_monthly_budget_usd.title: Monthly AI budget (USD)
dates_ai_monthly_budget_usd.purpose: The most the event AI may spend in a calendar month, in whole US dollars, counted from list prices.
dates_ai_monthly_budget_usd.effect: Each AI call reserves its estimated cost first. When the cap is reached, new intakes wait for budget and are retried hourly; at 80% the usage page shows an alert. 0 switches the AI off without touching the draft switch.
dates_ai_monthly_budget_usd.caution: Raising the cap lets waiting intakes continue within the hour. The figure is the console's own ledger, not the provider's invoice; compare the two before relying on it.

dates_ai_provider_order.title: AI provider order
dates_ai_provider_order.purpose: The order in which the AI providers are tried for an extraction: one to three of OpenAI, Google Gemini and Anthropic, each at most once.
dates_ai_provider_order.effect: The first provider is asked first; the next only when the one before returns no usable event, declines or is unavailable. A provider without a key on the server is skipped, and one left out of the list is never called.
dates_ai_provider_order.caution: A draft from a backup provider is marked as such for the reviewer. Changing the order changes where sources are sent, so it must match the processors named in the privacy notice.

dates_ai_openai_model.title: OpenAI model
dates_ai_openai_model.purpose: The OpenAI model that reads a source and drafts the event sheet.
dates_ai_openai_model.effect: The identifier is sent to the provider as it is. Each AI call records the model that actually answered, which is what the usage page and the intake show.
dates_ai_openai_model.caution: Core checks only the shape of the identifier. A model the key cannot use makes every OpenAI call answer as unavailable, so the next provider takes over; confirm the name in the provider's current documentation first.

dates_ai_openai_adjudication_model.title: OpenAI model for comparing events
dates_ai_openai_adjudication_model.purpose: The OpenAI model that is asked whether two drafts describe the same event when the deterministic comparison is not conclusive.
dates_ai_openai_adjudication_model.effect: Its answer only informs the duplicate check shown to the reviewer; it never rejects or merges anything by itself.
dates_ai_openai_adjudication_model.caution: It runs within the same monthly budget. A smaller, cheaper model is enough for this task; check the name in the provider's current documentation before changing it.

dates_ai_gemini_model.title: Google Gemini model
dates_ai_gemini_model.purpose: The Gemini model used when Gemini is the provider that answers an extraction.
dates_ai_gemini_model.effect: The identifier is sent to the provider as it is, and the model that actually answered is recorded with each call.
dates_ai_gemini_model.caution: Core checks only the shape of the identifier. Confirm the name in the provider's current documentation; an unknown model makes Gemini answer as unavailable.

dates_event_intake_retention_days.title: Intake content retention (days)
dates_event_intake_retention_days.purpose: How many days after a decision the flyers and source texts of an intake are kept, between 1 and 365.
dates_event_intake_retention_days.effect: After that the worker deletes the flyer files and the source texts; the decision record itself is kept 180 days for audit. The clock starts when an intake is published, rejected or otherwise finished.
dates_event_intake_retention_days.caution: Shortening it does not delete anything at once: the next run of the worker applies it. It must agree with the retention stated in the privacy notice.

dates_event_ticket_domains.title: Allowed ticketing sites
dates_event_ticket_domains.purpose: The ticketing sites a ticket link may point at besides the organizer's and the venue's own site: up to 50 lower-case host names.
dates_event_ticket_domains.effect: A ticket link found in a source is kept only on one of those sites; any other is dropped and the reviewer is told. The same list applies when an AI-drafted event is edited later.
dates_event_ticket_domains.caution: List only official ticket sellers, never resale sites. A host name has no https://, no path and no www. prefix. An empty list allows none.

dates_external_suggestions_enabled.title: Members' suggestions
dates_external_suggestions_enabled.purpose: Master switch of the channel through which members suggest events. Its default is OFF; only the exact stored boolean true turns it on.
dates_external_suggestions_enabled.effect: OFF refuses a new suggestion from the app, a question to the member and the publication of a member's suggestion. Suggestions already in the queue can still be read and rejected.
dates_external_suggestions_enabled.caution: Turn it on only when the AI intake works for administrators and reviewers are ready for the queue. It is independent of the administrators' draft switch and of the external-event publication switch.

dates_event_suggestion_daily_limit.title: Suggestions per member per day
dates_event_suggestion_daily_limit.purpose: How many suggestions one member may submit in a rolling 24 hours, between 1 and 50. The default is 5.
dates_event_suggestion_daily_limit.effect: Every accepted submission counts, whatever became of it. Over the limit a new suggestion is refused: nothing is stored and no AI call is made.
dates_event_suggestion_daily_limit.caution: Each suggestion costs an AI run. Raise the limit together with the monthly AI budget, not on its own.

dates_event_suggestion_monthly_limit.title: Suggestions per member per thirty days
dates_event_suggestion_monthly_limit.purpose: How many suggestions one member may submit in a rolling thirty days, between 1 and 500. The default is 20.
dates_event_suggestion_monthly_limit.effect: Counted like the daily limit. When both are reached the app is told about this one first, because it lasts longer.
dates_event_suggestion_monthly_limit.caution: It bounds how many AI runs a single account can cause in a month. Below the daily limit it is the only limit that ever applies.

dates_event_suggestion_open_limit.title: Open suggestions per member
dates_event_suggestion_open_limit.purpose: How many suggestions of one member may be open at once - being drafted, with the member, or in review - between 1 and 20. The default is 3.
dates_event_suggestion_open_limit.effect: A member at the limit cannot submit another until one of theirs is decided or withdrawn. A suggestion answered at once as a duplicate holds no open slot.
dates_event_suggestion_open_limit.caution: A low value keeps one member from filling the review queue; a value near the daily limit removes that protection.

dates_event_suggestion_strike_limit.title: Strikes before a suggestion ban
dates_event_suggestion_strike_limit.purpose: How many rejections as spam or fake, inside the strike window, ban a member from suggesting, between 1 and 20. The default is 3.
dates_event_suggestion_strike_limit.effect: Only a rejection with the reason spam or fake is a strike. A rejection that is under a second look is not counted until that look ends, and a second look that ends otherwise takes the strike back.
dates_event_suggestion_strike_limit.caution: A strike is a sanction against a member. Use the spam-or-fake reason only for that, and expect a member to ask for a second look.

dates_event_suggestion_strike_window_day.title: Strike window (days)
dates_event_suggestion_strike_window_day.purpose: Over how many days strikes are counted towards the limit, between 1 and 365. The default is 30.
dates_event_suggestion_strike_window_day.effect: A strike older than this no longer counts. The review screen shows the member's strikes inside the window beside the limit.
dates_event_suggestion_strike_window_day.caution: A longer window makes old rejections count for longer; a shorter one forgives them sooner. A ban that has already started keeps its end date.

dates_event_suggestion_ban_days.title: Suggestion ban (days)
dates_event_suggestion_ban_days.purpose: For how many days a member who reached the strike limit cannot suggest events, between 1 and 365. The default is 30.
dates_event_suggestion_ban_days.effect: During the ban the app refuses a new suggestion and says until when. The member can still withdraw a suggestion and ask for a second look at a rejection.
dates_event_suggestion_ban_days.caution: Changing it does not shorten or lengthen a ban that is already running: it applies to bans that start afterwards.

dates_event_suggestion_consent_version.title: Suggestion consent version
dates_event_suggestion_consent_version.purpose: The version of the consent text a member must have accepted before suggesting an event, between 1 and 1000. The default is 1.
dates_event_suggestion_consent_version.effect: Raising it makes every member accept the new text before their next suggestion; an acceptance of an older version is refused as outdated. Suggestions already submitted are not affected.
dates_event_suggestion_consent_version.caution: Raise it only together with a new consent text in the app, never to test: every member is asked again before their next suggestion.

dates_external_autopublish_enabled.title: Publication without a reviewer
dates_external_autopublish_enabled.purpose: Lets Core publish a member's suggestion by itself when every automatic check holds. Its default is OFF; only the exact stored boolean true turns it on.
dates_external_autopublish_enabled.effect: ON publishes a suggestion only when the whole allow-list holds for its single event, nothing suggests a duplicate, nobody is reviewing it, it is not a second look and its submitter has no strike. Such an event carries the tier its evidence supports and none of the four administrator confirmations.
dates_external_autopublish_enabled.caution: With this on, events reach members that no person has checked. Leave it off unless the owner has decided otherwise; three member reports pull such an event back like any other.

configuration.typesCopy: Stable keys with bilingual labels, order and active state. The final active type cannot be disabled.
configuration.retiredTypeCopy: The legacy type is no longer offered for new assignments. Existing activities remain readable and may keep their current type.
configuration.retirementPending: The stored catalogue still marks this type active. Save to persist its retirement in Core.
configuration.knownLimitationCopy: Account suspension cannot reliably prevent re-registration without identity verification.
configuration.reasonsCopy: Immutable reason IDs, keys and member/external-event groups, with editable bilingual copy, severity and entry points within the same group. Deactivation preserves history.
configuration.newReasonCopy: Adds a new versioned reason with a generated stable ID.
configuration.entryPointsHint: Available entry points: {values}. external_event is for activity reasons only and must be used alone. An existing reason cannot move between member and external-event groups.
configuration.entryPointsEmpty: Add at least one entry point for this scope.
configuration.entryPointsMixedExternal: Use external_event on its own. It cannot be combined with member-activity entry points.
configuration.entryPointsCohort: This reason cannot move between member activities and external events. Keep it in its original group.
configuration.entryPointsUnknown: Not an entry point for this scope: {values}. Use only: {allowed}.
configuration.entryPointsRefused: Core refused these entry points. Use only: {allowed}. external_event must stand alone, and an existing reason must stay in its original member or external-event group.
configuration.unknownTypeHelp: This console has no editor for this type of setting, so the value is shown read-only and cannot be saved from here. A newer Webadmin release is needed to change it.
configuration.stringHelp: Text. Core validates the value when it is saved.
configuration.modelIdHelp: The model identifier exactly as the provider writes it, for example gpt-6.1-sol: lower-case letters and digits, joined by dots, hyphens or underscores. Core checks only the shape; a model the key cannot use answers as unavailable and the next provider is tried.
configuration.modelIdInvalid: This does not look like a model identifier. Start with a lower-case letter and use only lower-case letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores, at most 64 characters.
configuration.orderedListLabel: Order in which they are tried
configuration.orderedListHelp: The first provider is asked first. The next one is tried only when the one before returns no usable event, declines or is unavailable - never because a draft failed validation. A provider left out is never called; at least one is required.
configuration.stringListHelp: One item per line. Core validates every item when the list is saved.
configuration.ticketDomainsHelp: One host name per line: lower-case, without https://, a path or www. - for example jegy.hu. A ticket link is kept only when it is on the organizer's or the venue's own site or on one of these. An empty list allows no ticketing site.

stringListProblems.count: The list must have between {minimum} and {maximum} items.
stringListProblems.value: An item is not one of the allowed values.
stringListProblems.length: An item is empty or longer than 253 characters.
stringListProblems.host: An item is not a plain host name: lower-case, no https://, no path, no www. prefix - for example jegy.hu.

configuration.consentVersionNoText: This version has no text yet. Core accepts only a consent version whose text exists in this release.

suggestionConsent.draftTitle: The suggestion terms are still a draft.
suggestionConsent.draft: Members are served version {version} of the terms, and counsel has not approved that text yet. Core does not stop the switch for it: decide knowing it.
suggestionConsent.approved: Version {version} of the terms is approved in every language members are served.
suggestionConsent.missing: Version {version} of the suggestion terms has no complete text in this release, so members cannot suggest events whatever this switch says. Set the required version to one that has a text, or release the text.
suggestionConsent.unreadable: The state of the suggestion terms' text could not be read. It is not known whether the text is approved.

intake.aiNotice: Everything on these pages was extracted by AI from a link, a flyer or a line of text. Nothing is published until a person has checked it against the source and published it. Members never see an intake.

queue.title: Intakes
queue.subtitle: Sources handed to the event AI and the drafts it made of them. A reviewer takes an intake, checks the draft against the source, then rejects it or publishes its events.
queue.draftsOff: Drafting from a source is switched off (dates_external_admin_drafts_enabled). No new intake can be created or published until an administrator turns it on in Configuration; the intakes already here can still be read and rejected.
queue.orderReview: Intakes in review are listed with the soonest event first.
queue.unreadableRow: Row {row} of this page could not be read and is not shown.
queue.emptyPage: This page has no intakes. The queue may have changed while loading; refresh or go back a page.
queue.suggestionsOff: Members' suggestions are switched off (dates_external_suggestions_enabled). Members cannot send new ones, and those already here cannot be published or sent back to the member until an administrator turns them on in Configuration; they can still be read and rejected.
queue.secondLooksWaiting: Second looks waiting for a reviewer: {count}. A member asked for the rejection of a suggestion to be looked at again.
queue.orderSecondLook: Second looks are listed with the oldest request first.

lease.title: Who is working on it
lease.copy: Taking an intake reserves it for you for five minutes, and the page keeps renewing that while it is open. Rejecting and publishing need your hold; nobody can take an intake from a reviewer whose time has not run out.
lease.unreadable: Core's answer about who holds this intake could not be read, so no action is offered. Refresh to read it again.
lease.uncertain: The outcome of this action is not known. The intake was read again; check who holds it before continuing.

done.claim: The intake is yours for the next five minutes.

access.denied: Your role does not include this. Reviewing intakes needs the event review capability, and the AI usage needs read access to external events. Nothing was hidden from you by an error.
access.refused: Core refused this request. Its answer is shown above.
access.unconfirmed: This could not be read. That says nothing about your permissions and does not mean there is nothing to show. Refresh to try again.
access.reviewRequired: Taking, rejecting and reading an intake need the event review capability.
access.manageRequired: You can review and reject, but publishing an event needs the event management capability of an administrator.

detail.title: Intake
detail.subtitle: The source, what the AI read from it, the evidence for each field and what Core's own checks say. Compare it with the source before you decide.
detail.progress: This page checks again by itself.
detail.unreadableSections: These parts of Core's answer could not be read and are not shown: {sections}. They are not empty; they are unknown.
detail.injection: The AI flagged text in the source that tries to give it instructions. Core used none of it, but read this draft with extra care.
detail.purgedAt: The flyers and source texts of this intake were deleted on {date}, as the retention setting requires. The record itself is kept for audit.
detail.retentionCopy: flyers and source texts until {content}; the record until {record}
detail.unreadableInputs: What was submitted could not be read from Core's answer.
detail.unreadableImages: Flyers that could not be read from Core's answer: {count}.
detail.flyerPrivate: Private evidence. The flyer is never published, never used as the event image, and every time it is shown here Core records who looked.
detail.flyerNotReady: The flyer is not available: Core has not re-encoded it yet, or it has been deleted.
detail.flyerAlt: Submitted flyer {index}, as Core re-encoded it
detail.flyerShow: Show the flyer (the view is recorded)
detail.unreadableTexts: Source texts that could not be read from Core's answer: {count}.
detail.unreadableRuns: AI calls that could not be read from Core's answer: {count}.
detail.noRuns: No AI call has been made for this intake.
detail.extractionTitle: What the AI made of it
detail.extractionNotice: This is an AI draft, not a fact. Each field below shows the words the AI quoted for it and whether Core found those words in the source. A field marked Unverified is the AI's claim alone.
detail.noEvents: The AI did not produce an event from this source.
detail.unreadableEvent: Event {index} could not be read from Core's answer. It is not shown and cannot be published from here.
detail.noControls: Core's revision or hold for this intake could not be read, so nothing can be changed from this page. Refresh to read it again.
detail.notValidated: Core has not validated this event yet.
detail.hardFails: It cannot be published as it stands:
detail.publicVenueConfirmation: The venue may be a private address. It can only be published if you confirm in the editor that it is a public place.
detail.evidenceTitle: Field by field: the AI's claim and its evidence
detail.noEvidence: Core has not checked the evidence of this event yet.
detail.unverifiedFields: Not verified against the source: {fields}. Check these yourself.
detail.allVerified: Core found the quoted words for every field in the source. That confirms what the source says, not that the source is right.
detail.checkNoQuote: The AI gave no quote for this field.
detail.checkFound: The quote is in the source ({match}).
detail.checkNotFound: The quote was not found in the source.
detail.denotesNot: The quote does not say this value.
detail.draftTitle: The rest of the AI's draft
detail.draftEnds: End, as the source states it
detail.publicVenueClaim: The AI considers the venue public
detail.yearInferred: The source gives no year; the AI assumed one.
detail.timeNotStated: The source states no start time.
detail.priceUnknown: The source does not say whether it is free.
detail.endEstimated: Not stated; Core would estimate it from the category
detail.venueUnresolved: Core could not resolve the venue to a place. Enter and confirm it by hand in the editor.
detail.similarity: Match with the venue in the source
detail.noWitness: The page carried no machine-readable event data to compare with.
detail.automaticTitle: Would it qualify for automatic publication?
detail.automaticYes: It meets every condition. Nothing acts on this: a person still reviews and publishes.
detail.automaticNo: No. Nothing acts on this either way; these are the conditions it misses:
detail.refreshFailed: The intake could not be read again just now. What you see may be out of date; nothing was changed. Try Refresh again.
detail.progressStopped: The worker is still on it. Use Refresh to see where it stands.
detail.notLinked: (not an https address: shown as text, not as a link)
detail.eventsUnreadable: The extracted events could not be read: Core served them in a shape this console does not know. They are not missing, and this does not mean the AI found no event. Nothing can be published from this page until the console can read them.
detail.runsUnreadable: The AI calls of this intake could not be read. That does not mean no AI call was made; the monthly figures are on the AI usage page.
detail.textsUnreadable: The text Core holds of the source could not be read. It is not empty; it is unknown.
detail.revisionUnreadable: The last read of this intake could not be used: Core served its revision in a shape this console does not know. The page shows the state it last read whole; your hold and the actions still work from that state. Refresh to try again.
detail.secondLook: Second look: the member asked for the rejection of this suggestion to be looked at again. The first decision is under "The member's side". Decide again by publishing an event of it or by rejecting it.
detail.suggestionsOff: Members' suggestions are switched off (dates_external_suggestions_enabled). This suggestion can be read and rejected, but not published and not sent back to the member, until an administrator turns them on.

checks.weekday_match: The weekday in the source matches the date
checks.venue_resolved: The venue was resolved to a place
checks.public_place: The place is a public venue
checks.tz_from_venue: The time zone comes from the venue
checks.urls_from_evidence: Every link appears in the sources
checks.quotes_verified: The date and time quotes were found in the source

editor.title: Check and publish
editor.unreadable: Core's prefill for this event could not be read, so it cannot be opened in the editor.
editor.noPrefill: Core offers no editor prefill for this event.
editor.holdFirst: Take the intake to publish from it.
editor.cannotPublish: Publishing is not available to you here: it needs the event management capability and the draft switch to be on.
editor.notice: The form is prefilled with the AI's draft. Correct every field against the source, tick the four confirmations yourself and give an audit reason. Publishing makes the event visible to members at once.
editor.formNotice: Prefilled by AI from the submitted source. Nothing here has been confirmed by a person yet; an empty field is one Core could not determine.
editor.gaps: Core could not fill these in; you have to: {fields}.
editor.complete: This is the last event I publish from this intake (the other {remaining} will not be published).
editor.confirm: You are publishing content an AI drafted and you have checked. The event appears for members immediately and is marked as AI-assisted.
editor.confirmPartial: The intake stays with you for its other events.
editor.unreadableSiblings: Events of this intake that this console could not read: {count}. They are unknown, not absent. Choose what happens to the intake when this event is published.
editor.keepOpen: Publish this event and leave the intake open, so that the unread events can still be reviewed once the console can read them.
editor.closeAnyway: Publish this event and close the intake, knowing that {count} unread and {remaining} other unpublished events will never be published from it.
editor.confirmCloseUnreadable: This closes the intake although {count} of its events could not be read. They will never be reviewed from it.
editor.changed: The intake changed after you prepared this publication: other events are now left, or one of them can no longer be read. Check the choice above and review the publication again.
editor.memberCredit: The event will name member #{uid} as the member who suggested it.
editor.memberAnonymous: The member asked not to be named: the event will not show who suggested it.
editor.memberGoing: The member asked to go: Core joins them with this publication if a join of their own would be allowed at that moment.
editor.memberGoingProgramme: The member asked to go, but this suggestion holds more than one event: Core joins a member only to a single-event suggestion.
editor.memberErased: The member's account was erased: the event carries no submitter.
editor.memberUnreadable: The member's choices (credit, going) could not be read on this page. Core applies them as it stored them.
editor.cannotPublishSuggestion: Publishing is not available to you here: it needs the event management capability and the members' suggestion switch to be on.
editor.memberSecondLookStrikeTakenBack: The first decision rejected this suggestion as spam or fake, which counted a strike against the member. Publishing it takes that strike back, and can end a ban it caused.

reject.title: Reject the intake
reject.copy: A rejection ends the intake. Pick the reason; the statement of reasons is Core's fixed wording for that reason, not free text.
reject.holdFirst: Take the intake to reject it.
reject.afterPublish: An event of this intake has already been published, so it can no longer be rejected. Finish it from the editor instead.
reject.statementHint: The submitter is shown Core's statement for this reason.
reject.noteHint: Kept in the audit log only; never shown to the submitter.
reject.confirm: Reject this intake with the reason below? This cannot be undone from the console.
reject.invalid: Choose a reason and write an audit note first.
reject.uncertain: It is not known whether the rejection landed. The intake was read again: if it is still in review, send the same rejection again; it cannot be applied twice.
reject.eventsUnreadable: The extracted events could not be read on this page. If you reject now, you decide without having seen what the AI extracted. Prefer leaving the intake until the console can read it.
reject.someUnreadable: Events of this intake that could not be read: {count}. A rejection covers them too, although you have not seen them.
reject.duplicateOfHint: The id of the event that is already listed (xev_ and 32 characters). With it the intake ends as a duplicate of that event; without it, as a rejection with the reason "duplicate".
reject.duplicateInvalid: This is not an event id: xev_ followed by 32 characters (0-9, a-f).
reject.doneDuplicate: The intake was closed as a duplicate of the event named.
reject.memberStatement: The member is notified and is shown Core's statement of reasons for this reason.
reject.memberDuplicate: The member is told that the event is already listed and is taken to it. Unless they asked not to be named, they are recorded on that event beside its first submitter.
reject.strike: Rejecting as spam or fake is a strike against the member. They have {strikes} of {limit} inside the window now; at the limit they are banned from suggesting.
reject.strikeUnknown: Rejecting as spam or fake is a strike against the member. Their current standing could not be read on this page.
reject.strikeNobody: The member's account was erased: this rejection is a strike against nobody.
reject.secondLook: This is the second look the member asked for. A second look can be asked for only once: rejecting again ends the suggestion.
reject.secondLookStrikeKept: The first decision already counted a strike against the member for this suggestion. Rejecting it as spam or fake again keeps that one strike and adds no new one.
reject.secondLookStrikeTakenBack: The first decision rejected this suggestion as spam or fake, which counted a strike against the member. Rejecting it now for another reason takes that strike back, and can end a ban it caused.

publish.done: The event is published and the intake is finished.
publish.donePartial: The event is published. The intake is still yours for its other events.
publish.doneRetained: Core published the event, but the saved request could not be cleared from this browser. Restore browser storage access and retry the same request to reconcile it.
publish.refusedRetained: Core refused the publication, but the saved request could not be cleared from this browser. Restore browser storage access and retry the same request; do not start a new one yet.
publish.uncertain: The publication may have succeeded, but its receipt did not arrive. The exact request is saved. Retry the same request; do not publish the event again.
publish.blocked: The publication could not safely proceed. Check the saved-operation panel and browser storage before retrying.
publish.expired: This saved request is too old for a safe retry. Do not delete it or publish again; ask the operations lead to reconcile the event with the audit log first.
publish.access: Your current permissions or Core's time could not be confirmed. Nothing was sent. Refresh and try again.
publish.invalid: The console would not send this request. Check the facts, the audit reason and the four confirmations.

source.title: Draft from source
source.copy: Give the AI a link, a flyer photo or a line of text. It drafts the event sheet; you review the draft and publish it through the usual editor. The AI never publishes.
source.disabled: Drafting from a source is switched off (dates_external_admin_drafts_enabled). An administrator can turn it on in
source.unknown: Whether drafting is switched on could not be read. You can try; Core answers if it is off.
source.urlHint: The organizer's or the venue's own page works best. Pages behind a login (Facebook, Instagram) cannot be read.
source.imagesHint: JPEG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC, at most 10 MiB each. The photo is sent as it is; Core removes its metadata and keeps it privately.
source.imageText: A line of text to go with the flyer (optional)
source.text: A line of text about the event
source.textHint: At most {maximum} characters. Name the event, the day, the time and the venue if you know them.
source.privacy: The source goes to the AI provider set in Configuration. Do not submit photos of people or private addresses. A flyer is never published and never becomes the event image.
source.uncertain: It is not known whether the draft was created: the answer did not arrive, or it does not say. Send the same source again now: while this panel is open it goes out as the same request, which finds the draft if it was made and cannot create a second one.

problems.url: Enter a full web address starting with http:// or https://.
problems.imageSize: A photo is empty or larger than 10 MiB.
problems.imageType: A file is not a JPEG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC image.

source.hint: Your submission at {time} ({kind}) got no answer, so it may or may not have arrived. You can look for it in the queue, or simply submit the same source again: while its draft is open, Core takes you to that draft instead of making a second one.
source.existing: This source had already been submitted by you, and its draft is still open: this is that draft, as it is now. Nothing new was created and no second AI run was started.

usage.title: AI usage
usage.subtitle: What the event AI has cost this month against the monthly cap, by provider, model, task and channel. Usage figures only: no source, no prompt, no content.
usage.monthHint: Leave empty for the current month, as Core counts it (UTC).
usage.capZero: The monthly cap is 0, so the AI is switched off: no AI call is made and new intakes wait for budget.
usage.exhausted: The monthly cap is used up. No further AI call is made this month; new intakes wait for budget until the cap is raised or the month ends.
usage.alert: More than 80% of the monthly cap has been spent.
usage.ofCap: {share} of the {cap} cap, with what is reserved
usage.awaitingBudgetHint: intakes the worker will retry when there is budget
usage.awaitingBudgetUnread: the review queue could not be read
usage.progress: Share of the monthly cap spent or reserved
usage.breakdown: By provider, model, task and channel
usage.breakdownHint: The model shown is the one that actually answered. Costs are computed from list prices and are not an invoice.
usage.unreadableRows: Rows that could not be read and are not shown: {count}.
usage.empty: No AI call was recorded in this month.
usage.ambiguousTitle: Calls whose cost is not known
usage.ambiguous: {count} AI calls this month may have been charged by the provider: each was sent, and its answer never arrived or could not be settled. Core counts such a call as spent at its whole reservation - {amount} in all. That money is in the spend above and counts against the cap, although it is not known whether the provider charged it.
usage.ambiguousListedSome: Newest first; Core lists {shown} of the {count}.
usage.ambiguousUnreadable: The calls whose cost is not known could not be read. The spend above is Core's own figure and includes them; it is not known how many there are.
usage.ambiguousUnreadableRuns: Listed calls that could not be read and are not shown: {count}.

ambiguousColumns.why: Why the cost is not known

ambiguousSources.transport: The request was sent to the provider, and what it cost could not be read from what came back.
ambiguousSources.unsettled: The call failed in the worker before its cost could be settled.
ambiguousSources.reaped: The worker stopped while the call was outstanding; Core's clean-up counted it.

ambiguousFailures.curl: The connection failed after the request was sent ({code}).
ambiguousFailures.no-usage: The provider answered, but its answer said nothing of what it used.
ambiguousFailures.response-too-large: The answer was too large to read.

statusHelp.received: Core has stored the source. The intake worker has not picked it up yet.
statusHelp.screening: The flyer is being re-encoded and screened, or the page is being fetched. No AI has been called yet.
statusHelp.extracting: The AI is reading the source and drafting the event sheet.
statusHelp.validating: Core is checking the draft: quotes, date and time, venue, time zone, links and duplicates.
statusHelp.member_confirming: The member who suggested the event is checking the draft.
statusHelp.in_review: The draft is ready for a person. Take the intake, compare the draft with the source, then reject it or publish its events.
statusHelp.published: An event was published from this intake; it is finished. The decision below says by whom.
statusHelp.merged: The source was attached to an event that already exists.
statusHelp.rejected: The intake was rejected and is finished.
statusHelp.duplicate: This source or this event is already here, so no AI was spent on it again. Open the original instead.
statusHelp.failed: The pipeline could not finish. The reason is shown below; nothing was published. Submit the source again if the cause was temporary.
statusHelp.withdrawn: The member withdrew the suggestion, or the member's account was erased.
statusHelp.expired: Nobody decided before the event started, or the wait for budget ran out. Nothing was published.
statusHelp.awaiting_budget: The monthly AI budget is used up or set to zero. The worker tries again every hour; raise the cap in Configuration to continue sooner.

statusDetailHelp.image-empty: The uploaded file had no content. Upload the photo again.
statusDetailHelp.image-unreadable: Core could not decode the file as an image. Try a JPEG or PNG copy of the flyer.
statusDetailHelp.image-too-large: The file is larger than 10 MiB.
statusDetailHelp.image-dimensions: The image is too small or has more pixels than Core accepts.
statusDetailHelp.image-encode-failed: Core could not write its own clean copy of the flyer.
statusDetailHelp.image-content-rejected: Content screening found likely adult or violent content, so the flyer was rejected before any AI was called.
statusDetailHelp.screening-unavailable: The content screening service did not answer. The worker tries again by itself.
statusDetailHelp.image-missing: The stored flyer file is no longer there.
statusDetailHelp.source-not-readable: The page is behind a login and cannot be read. Use the organizer's or the venue's own page.
statusDetailHelp.source-not-fetchable: Core does not fetch this address: it is not a public web address.
statusDetailHelp.source-unreachable: The page did not answer, or answered with an error.
statusDetailHelp.source-not-text: The address does not serve a web page Core can read.
statusDetailHelp.source-too-large: The page is larger than Core reads.
statusDetailHelp.source-empty: The page had no readable text.
statusDetailHelp.not-an-event: The AI concluded that the source does not describe an event people can attend.
statusDetailHelp.prohibited-category: The event belongs to a category that is not listed here.
statusDetailHelp.ai-unavailable: No AI provider answered. The worker tries again by itself; if this stays, check the provider order and the keys.
statusDetailHelp.ai-refused: The AI provider declined to process this source.
statusDetailHelp.ai-not-configured: No AI provider in the configured order has a key on the server.
statusDetailHelp.venue-search-unavailable: The place search did not answer, so the venue could not be resolved. Enter it by hand in the editor.
statusDetailHelp.duplicate-source: The same address was already submitted; no AI was spent on it again.
statusDetailHelp.duplicate-event: Core found the same event among the published events or the open intakes.
statusDetailHelp.start-passed: The event started before anyone decided: an undecided intake expired, and a partly published programme was closed with what had been published.
statusDetailHelp.storage-unavailable: Core's private storage for flyers is not available.
statusDetailHelp.attempts-exhausted: The same step failed six times in a row, so Core gave up.
statusDetailHelp.account-erased: The member who submitted this erased their account.
statusDetailHelp.ai-budget-overrun: A provider billed more for this intake than its per-call limit allows, so the intake failed. Nothing was published.

rejectReasons.unverifiable: Cannot be verified from a reliable source
rejectReasons.sensitive_not_allowed: Sensitive topic that is not listed
rejectReasons.spam_or_fake: Spam or not a genuine event

resultValues.prohibited: A category that is not allowed

hardFails.not_an_event: The source does not describe an event.
hardFails.prohibited_category: The event is in a category that is not allowed.
hardFails.insufficient_information: The source does not say enough to make an event of it.
hardFails.time_missing: The source states no start time.
hardFails.midnight_unconfirmed: The start is midnight, and the source does not confirm that.
hardFails.relative_date_unconfirmed: The date is relative (for example "on Saturday") and cannot be tied to a calendar day with certainty.
hardFails.local_time_nonexistent: That local time does not exist on that day (clock change).
hardFails.local_time_ambiguous: That local time occurs twice on that day (clock change).
hardFails.start_in_past: The start is in the past.
hardFails.start_beyond_lookahead: The start is further ahead than events may be entered.
hardFails.end_not_after_start: The end is not after the start.
hardFails.duration_too_long: The event is longer than allowed.
hardFails.weekday_mismatch: The weekday in the source does not match the date.
hardFails.venue_not_public: The venue is not a public place.
hardFails.venue_unresolved: The venue could not be resolved to a place.
hardFails.venue_ambiguous: Several places match the venue equally well.
hardFails.venue_country_unavailable: The venue is in a country where AreYouIn external events are not available.
hardFails.timezone_unknown: The time zone of the venue is not known.

warnings.prompt_injection_suspected: The source contains text that tries to instruct the AI.
warnings.fallback_provider: The backup AI provider answered, not the first one.
warnings.year_inferred: The source gives no year; it was assumed.
warnings.start_is_doors_time: The start time may be the doors-open time, not the start of the programme.
warnings.end_estimated: The end is not stated; it would be estimated from the category.
warnings.date_ambiguous: The date can be read in more than one way.
warnings.low_confidence_date: The AI is not confident about the date.
warnings.low_confidence_time: The AI is not confident about the time.
warnings.low_confidence_venue: The AI is not confident about the venue.
warnings.date_quote_unverified: The quote for the date was not found in the source.
warnings.time_quote_unverified: The quote for the time was not found in the source.
warnings.quotes_unverified: Some quotes were not found in the source.
warnings.witness_disagrees_date: The page's own event data gives a different date.
warnings.witness_disagrees_time: The page's own event data gives a different time.
warnings.witness_disagrees_venue: The page's own event data gives a different venue.
warnings.venue_similarity_low: The place found does not match the venue's name well.
warnings.possible_private_address: The venue may be a private address.
warnings.venue_unbounded: The venue could not be checked against a city or an area.
warnings.venue_unclear: The source is unclear about the venue.
warnings.paid_without_official_link: A paid event with no official link.
warnings.status_canceled: The source says the event is canceled.
warnings.status_postponed: The source says the event is postponed.

warnings.low_legibility: The flyer is hard to read.
warnings.language_uncertain: The language of the source is uncertain.
warnings.content_unscreened: The flyer was not screened for content.

autoBlockers.time_explicit: the start time is not stated explicitly
autoBlockers.confident: the AI is not confident enough
autoBlockers.venue_place_matches: the venue does not match a place closely enough
autoBlockers.timezone_known: the time zone is not known

dedupeValues.new: New: nothing like it was found.
dedupeValues.review: Possibly a duplicate: compare with the candidates.

linkDropReasons.not_in_sources: it does not appear in the sources
linkDropReasons.not_https: it is not an https address
linkDropReasons.domain_not_allowed: its site is not an allowed ticketing site

refusals.unknown: Core refused this request with a reason this console has no explanation for:
refusals.dates-intake-admin-drafts-disabled: Drafting from a source is switched off. An administrator turns it on in Configuration (dates_external_admin_drafts_enabled).
refusals.dates-intake-conflict: The intake changed since this page read it. It was read again; look at it before repeating the action.
refusals.dates-intake-event-unavailable: That event of the intake is not there, or has already been published.
refusals.dates-intake-filter-invalid: Core does not accept this filter.
refusals.dates-intake-id-invalid: This is not an intake identifier.
refusals.dates-intake-image-invalid: Core did not accept the photo: it must be a JPEG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC image of at most 10 MiB and at most two photos.
refusals.dates-intake-image-unavailable: The flyer is not available: it has not been re-encoded yet, or it has been deleted.
refusals.dates-intake-input-invalid: Core did not accept the request as it was sent: give exactly one source of the chosen kind.
refusals.dates-intake-kind-invalid: Core does not know this kind of source.
refusals.dates-intake-lease-invalid: Core does not know this hold action.
refusals.dates-intake-lease-lost: Your hold on this intake ran out. Take it again to continue.
refusals.dates-intake-lease-owner-required: Another reviewer holds this intake, and only they or a superadmin can release it.
refusals.dates-intake-lease-required: You have to hold the intake to do this. Take it first.
refusals.dates-intake-locale-invalid: Core does not accept this language.
refusals.dates-intake-origin-invalid: Core does not accept this location hint.
refusals.dates-intake-reason-invalid: Core does not know this rejection reason.
refusals.dates-intake-revision-invalid: The revision sent with the request is not valid. Refresh the page.
refusals.dates-intake-source-not-readable: That site is behind a login and cannot be read. Use the organizer's or the venue's own page instead.
refusals.dates-intake-state-invalid: The intake is no longer in a state that allows this.
refusals.dates-intake-storage-unavailable: Core's private storage for flyers is not available. Try again later.
refusals.dates-intake-text-invalid: Core did not accept the text: between 1 and 500 characters.
refusals.dates-intake-url-invalid: Core does not accept this address: it must be a public http or https web address.
refusals.dates-admin-capability-required: Your role does not allow this.
refusals.dates-admin-reason-invalid: The audit note is not acceptable: at most 1000 characters.
refusals.dates-admin-idempotency-invalid: The request identity is not valid. Refresh the page and try again.
refusals.dates-admin-idempotency-conflict: A different request was already sent with this identity. Refresh the page and start again.
refusals.dates-admin-command-in-progress: The same request is still being processed. Wait a moment and retry it.
refusals.dates-admin-unavailable: Core could not process the request. Try again later.
refusals.dates-external-publishing-disabled: Publishing external events is switched off by the release switch. Only the release lead turns it on.
refusals.dates-external-duplicate: The same event is already published: the same source and day, or the same title, venue and day.
refusals.dates-external-confirmation-required: All four confirmations have to be ticked.
refusals.dates-external-input-invalid: Core did not accept the event sheet as it was sent.
refusals.dates-external-start-invalid: The start is in the past or further ahead than events may be entered.
refusals.dates-external-duration-invalid: The end is not after the start, or the event is longer than allowed.
refusals.dates-external-venue-invalid: The venue is incomplete or not valid.
refusals.dates-external-url-invalid: A link is not a valid https address.
refusals.dates-external-ticket-domain-invalid: The ticket link is not on the organizer's site or an allowed ticketing site.
refusals.dates-external-paid-official-link-requir: A paid event needs an official link.
refusals.dates-external-summary-invalid: A summary is missing or too long.
refusals.dates-external-organizer-invalid: The organizer is missing or not valid.
refusals.dates-external-price-invalid: The price text is not valid.
refusals.dates-external-age-invalid: The age limit must be between 18 and 99.
refusals.dates-external-sensitive-invalid: A sensitive event needs a reason.
refusals.dates-external-attendee-list-invalid: The attendee list setting is not valid.
refusals.dates-timezone-invalid: The time zone is not a valid IANA name.
refusals.dates-title-invalid: The title must be between 3 and 120 characters.
refusals.unauthorized: Core did not accept the console's credential.

refusals.auth-required: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
refusals.invalid-input: The console did not send this request because it was not in the expected form.
refusals.image-too-large: A photo is larger than 10 MiB.
refusals.image-type-unsupported: A file is not a JPEG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC image.
